articles.title: Falkirk brick wall Scott Bain boosts Scotland credentials
articles.summary: Scott Bain proved unbeatable as he helped Falkirk defeat his former club, Celtic, just in time for the goalkeeper to push his case for inclusion in the latest Scotland squad.
articles.body:
Scott Bain must be praying that Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli was watching on as Falkirk ended a 19-year wait to beat Celtic.

The former Celtic goalkeeper was imperious, unbeatable, as Falkirk ran out 2-0 winners to earn a fourth win on the bounce and reach fourth place in the Scottish Premiership.

An absolute brick wall as he earned a third clean sheet in a row.

Not that all the praise should go his way. Everyone in Bairns blue delivered, but Bain was inspired, making save after save to deny Celtic on a day that will go down in Falkirk folklore. One that intensified the pressure on Martin O'Neill's side.

With the Scotland squad for the upcoming Nations League fixtures announced this week, surely Bain has enhanced his chances of pushing for not just a place in the squad but potentially the chance to stake a claim for a starting role.

Listen: Derby delight for Hibs, fresh questions for Celtic

Are Celtic club in regression amid run of six defeats in 10?

Impressive Falkirk earn first win over hapless Celtic in 19 years

'Unbelievable' Bain stands out between the sticks

Bain made nine saves against Celtic, with a number of them outstanding, as his side kept a clean sheet for the third game in a row.

That's now a run of 342 minutes without conceding a goal for the Bairns.

"Scott Bain was unbelievable," former Celtic goalkeeper Pat Bonner enthused. "Absolutely unbelievable.

"It was a terrific display from Falkirk defensively. Falkirk deserve it. They've got a terrific young team."

Bain himself explained how he felt as he zoned in on repelling Celtic no matter what they threw at him.

"I felt really confident in the game," he said. "I felt confident in the players and the game plan and I knew that I would be called upon, but it just felt like one of those days where they weren't going to score.

"You can't really get a better day as a goalkeeper than thinking that you're not going to be beaten. So, really, really pleased for my own performance, but more so pleased for the team. It's a fantastic step in the right direction."

Bain a bedrock in Falkirk's rise under McGlynn

The Scotland international extended his Falkirk contract in January and is tied to the club until the summer of 2028, with the option of a further year.

At the time, manager John McGlynn stated that "he's been outstanding from the moment he walked into the club".

After this fabulous display, he lavished even more praise on his number one, who turns 35 this month.

"Scott Bain had two really outstanding saves [in the first half] and there might have been another very good save, but there weren't as many as there were in the second half where he had to continuously produce," he said.

"So a huge thank you to Scott for the actual game he's had today."

No talk of that just being his job but genuine thanks for a memorable afternoon that went a long way to delivering a memorable win.

Bain took a step out of his comfort zone as back-up at Celtic. A sizeable drop in salary to pursue his ambition of regular game time. Days like this surely make that decision justified.

With Scotland lacking the sort of goalkeeping depth they enjoyed for so many years, displays like this can certainly do no harm.

There's an argument that Bain, outside of his shot-stopping ability that was on full display against Celtic, has the type of composure with his feet that may suit Pocognoli's approach.

"I think I've performed well since the last camp and I think I've been performing well throughout the season," Bain added.

"So I would hope to be in it [Scotland squad]. I really enjoyed the last camp. I really enjoyed the way the manager worked and seeing what he wants from his team.

"I'd be delighted if I can get back in and experience more time with him."

This time, the four-time capped goalkeeper may have enhanced his chances of adding to that tally.

articles.title: Ten Hag señala con dardo: "Desde que el Madrid vende a Cristiano, fue su fin..."
articles.standfirst: El técnico neerlandés recuerda su tensa convivencia con el portugués en Manchester y asegura que el Real Madrid acertó al venderlo en 2018
articles.summary: El técnico neerlandés recuerda su tensa convivencia con el portugués en Manchester y asegura que el Real Madrid acertó al venderlo en 2018
articles.body: Erik ten Hag ha vuelto a señalar a Cristiano Ronaldo. El neerlandés repasó en el programa Goedemorgen Eredivisie, de ESPN, los meses que compartieron en el Manchester United en 2022. Una relación breve, con tensiones y un desencuentro que terminó con la rescisión del contrato del portugués en noviembre de aquel año. Su diagnóstico sobre el rendimiento del delantero fue contundente: "La realidad es que en los últimos siete u ocho años ya no ha podido ofrecer ese nivel. Desde la Juventus ya se había acabado". El actual director técnico del FC Twente situó el origen del problema en el encaje de la estrella dentro del conjunto. "Todo gran equipo debe arropar a su mejor jugador, pero el mejor jugador también debe ceder ante el equipo. Ese era precisamente el problema con Ronaldo", explicó. Ten Hag quiso dejar claro el lugar que concede al portugués en la historia del fútbol: "Que no haya ningún malentendido por mi parte: es, por supuesto, un jugador extraordinario. Está entre los más grandes". El Real Madrid también apareció en su análisis. Para Ten Hag, el club blanco eligió el momento adecuado para cerrar la etapa de Cristiano, que abandonó el Santiago Bernabéu en 2018 rumbo a la Juventus. "Ese es también el gran don del Real Madrid. Ven cuándo un jugador empieza a bajar de nivel. Entonces se despiden de él en un momento en el que, para el mundo exterior, todavía está en su apogeo, aunque en realidad ya no pueda ofrecer ese rendimiento", aseguró. En su etapa a las órdenes del neerlandés, Ronaldo, entonces de 37 años, marcó tres goles en 16 partidos. Hans Kraay jr., presente en el programa, le preguntó si hubo también momentos de buena sintonía entre ambos. La respuesta apenas dejó espacio para la nostalgia: "No, fue un periodo muy corto. Había tensión". El entrenador relacionó aquellas dificultades con la preparación física y con las exigencias de la competición inglesa. "Ya no era capaz de obligarse a sufrir. De darlo todo cada día. De ponerse en forma. Si no estás en forma en la Premier League, no tienes ninguna posibilidad", afirmó Ten Hag. El neerlandés reconoció que Cristiano conserva su capacidad para resolver delante de la portería: "Todavía puede aprovechar las ocasiones. Eso se sigue viendo. Pero si ya no puedes llegar al área…". El técnico también contó cómo abordó aquellas conversaciones con el delantero. "Le pones delante de un espejo y le presentas argumentos sólidos. Entonces todo queda muy claro", relató. Kraay jr. le planteó si Ronaldo había reaccionado diciéndole que no estaba bien de la cabeza. Ten Hag lo negó: "No, no dice eso en absoluto. Las pruebas eran muy claras. Hoy en día se registra todo en el fútbol". Ten Hag recordó los méritos del portugués para explicar la dimensión de las decisiones que tuvo que tomar. "Ha ganado cinco veces la Champions League y ha marcado muchísimos goles. Le ha dado muchísimo al fútbol. Todos hemos disfrutado con él, yo también. Pero en aquel momento tenía que tomar decisiones en beneficio del equipo y del club". A su juicio, el siguiente paso dependía del propio futbolista: "Al final, la elección era suya. Si quería hacer ese esfuerzo. Si no quiere hacerlo, tengo que tomar otras decisiones en interés del club. Eso es lo que vimos". El neerlandés fue preguntado por la dificultad de sentar en el banquillo a Cristiano e incluso dejarlo fuera de alguna convocatoria. Respondió con el criterio que, según explicó, guio su gestión de aquel vestuario: "Nadie es más grande que un club o un país. Cristiano Ronaldo tampoco. Messi tampoco. Al final, el equipo siempre está por delante".

articles.title: Harry Kane penalty miss mars Ballon d'Or week with Bayern Munich plus Twente score NINE in the Euro Debrief
articles.summary: Harry Kane's post-Ballon d'Or career did not start well for Bayern Munich. Adam Bate was there to see it and picks out the big stories from the continent in the Euro Debrief, a Sky Sports column focusing on the major European leagues and more...
articles.body:
Welcome to The Euro Debrief , the Sky Sports column in which Adam Bate rounds up some of the key stories from the latest matches across the continent. This week:

PSG's 'reserves' top the table in France

It was all set up for Harry Kane to star for Bayern Munich in Der Klassiker against Borussia Dortmund. Instead, in his first appearance since winning the Ballon d'Or, his penalty miss proved costly as Fabio Silva snatched a point in the Allianz Arena.

It was a strange spectacle being in Munich at the weekend. The Bayern fans had a banner declaring Kane 'no showman, but a footballer as he should be' and yet the club understandably did feel compelled to put on a show in celebrating his individual prize.

When the line-ups appeared on the big screen before kick-off, Kane's avatar was in gold, clutching the Ballon d'Or. He came out separately to the tune of Land of Hope and Glory from Edward Elgar's Pomp and Circumstance March No.1 and gave a brief speech.

Kane has been open about being out of his comfort zone and for a man so meticulous in his preparation, one did wonder as he picked grass from the golden studs on the sole of his specially-made boots before his penalty whether all this has been a distraction.

What was impressive was that he is always willing to front up. After taking all of the plaudits this past week, there must have been a temptation to shy away from the questions after being largely culpable for two dropped points against Bayern's big rivals.

But there he was talking to the assembled media again afterwards, taking the responsibility for the draw. "We definitely had enough chances to win the game. Me on my own had enough chances to win the game, but it was not to be," he admitted.

"Obviously, today wasn't my best performance or the team's best performance but that's life, that's part of being a striker, being a footballer. I could have probably been out there for another hour today and the ball would not have gone in the back of the net.

"You have to take that on the chin sometimes." Not the way Kane would have wanted such a wonderful week to end, then, but a reminder of how this world can bite even the best on the backside. Expect him to bounce back but maybe without those gold boots.

If it was a disappointing weekend for the Bundesliga top scorer of the past three seasons, it was another good one for the man who is currently on course to take his crown this time around. Niclas Fullkrug scored again for Werder Bremen in a 2-0 win.

Hoffenheim became the seventh team in succession to fail to keep out the 33-year-old striker who is enjoying a spectacular renaissance in his second spell with the club. His team are up fifth in the table after Bayer Leverkusen were beaten at home to Stuttgart.

Bundesliga results: Elversberg 4-1 Mainz, Augsburg 1-2 Freiburg, Bayer Leverkusen 2-4 Stuttgart, Borussia Monchengladbach 0-0 Paderborn, Schalke 0-2 RB Leipzig, Werder Bremen 2-0 Hoffenheim, Bayern Munich 2-2 Borussia Dortmund, Union Berlin 1-1 Cologne, Eintracht Frankfurt 3-1 Hamburg.

Defeats to Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid will surely have been a blow to Barcelona's belief that they can beat the best under Hansi Flick but when it comes to tearing the rest of the teams apart there is no better outfit in European football.

Alaves copped for six goals at Camp Nou on Saturday with Raphinha and Lamine Yamal registering two apiece before Anthony Gordon came off the bench to score too. Barca have now scored 46 goals in 11 LaLiga games - on course for 159 in a 38-game season.

Real Madrid's win over Racing Santander was similarly routine as Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Yan Diomande all scored in the first half. With Arda Guler impressing from the right, there is a growing feeling that this could be their best attacking quartet.

That might sound strange with Vinicius Junior absent but Diomande looks excellent playing from the left and has now scored or assisted in each of his last six games for the club. Has Jose Mourinho found his best combination? Awkward conversations ahead.

Atletico Madrid, meanwhile, are showing that there is more than one way to win football matches. Their 2-0 win away to Levante means that Diego Simeone's side have won seven games in a row now in LaLiga and stay two points behind Barcelona in second.

While Barca have scored more than twice as many goals as Atletico, it is Simeone's side who boast the best defensive record in the competition. Unstoppable forces, immovable objects and all that? We will know more when Atleti host Barca next Sunday.

That is the big game in LaLiga next weekend but this time around it was in Bilbao where Athletic Club took on Real Sociedad in the Basque Derby. The home side won 2-1 but it was not without controversy with Athletic lucky to get the deciding penalty.

It was amazing that VAR did not overturn the call against Jon Aramburu for a foul on Nico Williams when Williams himself did not think it was a penalty and Athletic boss Edin Terzic admitted things went their way. A disappointing way to decide a special fixture.

LaLiga results: Villarreal 0-1 Espanyol, Levante 0-2 Atletico Madrid, Rayo Vallecano 3-0 Celta Vigo, Real Betis 2-1 Malaga, Barcelona 6-1 Alaves, Getafe 3-1 Sevilla, Racing Santander 0-3 Real Madrid, Elche 0-1 Valencia, Athletic Club 2-1 Real Sociedad.

Inter were beaten for the first time in Serie A this season in the showpiece game in Italy, losing the Derby della Madonnina to Milan. The 3-1 result is massive for Ruben Amorim and owed much to the efforts of Diego Moreira, their summer signing from Strasbourg.

Moreira scored the first free-kick by a Milan player in this Serie A fixture since Andrea Pirlo almost two decades ago and set up the other two goals. Milan did the double over Inter last season too and it did not deny their rivals the title but this could be different.

That is because Inter are three points adrift of leaders Lazio after Gennaro Gattuso's team came from behind to beat Cagliari in the Stadio Olimpico. The strange alchemy happening at Lazio continued as substitute Andrea Pinamonti headed in a late winner.

It is six consecutive wins now and, not for the first time this season, the underlying numbers suggested that Lazio did not have the best of the chances. But 10 games in and they are still undefeated - with Roma the only other side who can say the same.

Gian Piero Gasperini's side overwhelmed Udinese, winning 5-2 having been four up at half-time with Donyell Malen netting again. Roma are Serie A's top scorers. One way or another, the title could be going to the capital for the first time in a quarter of a century.

Serie A results: Bologna 2-1 Monza, Udinese 2-5 Roma, Milan 3-1 Inter, Como 1-0 Venezia, Frosinone 2-0 Torino, Lazio 2-1 Cagliari, Lecce 1-2 Genoa, Juventus 2-0 Napoli.

It was not the best week in Ligue 1 for those hoping for a title race to emerge as Paris Saint-Germain provided an ominous reminder of their superiority. Yet another heavily rotated PSG line-up won 5-1 at Le Havre without many of their most famous names.

Achraf Hakimi was present and duly scored three goals as Luis Enrique's side made it nine wins out of nine in all competitions - including those European victories of Manchester City and Barcelona. They top the table in France after that early wobble.

Lille did at least score late through the veteran Olivier Giroud to stay within two points but Rennes conceded five times at Nice to lose ground. Cameron Archer found the net yet again for Auxerre but it was their only goal among the six scored in Strasbourg.

Marseille are up to sixth, while Paris FC were also big movers, beating Monaco 3-1 to leapfrog both them and Rennes into fourth. If Liam Rosenior secures Champions League football for next season it would be huge for the club and the rebuilding of his reputation.

Ligue 1 results: Le Havre 1-5 Paris Saint-Germain, Nice 5-2 Rennes, Lille 1-0 Lens, Troyes 2-0 Le Mans, Strasbourg 5-1 Auxerre, Lyon 2-0 Angers, Paris FC 3-1 Monaco, Marseille 2-0 Toulouse.

The biggest win of the weekend on the continent belonged to FC Twente as they pumped Excelsior 9-0 away from home. Their hosts were down to 10 men for all but five minutes of the match but it is still a remarkable feat with Wout Weghorst scoring four.

Over in Portugal, Porto stay perfect at the top of the table with a comfortable victory that means they have won 10 out of 10 so far. Benfica and Sporting both won too, and a word for Sporting's Pedro Lima, once of Norwich, who scored his first league goal for the club.

A graduate of Palmeiras' academy, he also scored two on his full debut in midweek and is an interesting character having studied for a philosophy degree in Brazil. His 89-year-old grandmother was in the stands for his first start. And it has been some start indeed.

articles.title: Fabio Silva is Borussia Dortmund's hero in Der Klassiker: Could the Portugal forward fulfil his potential after all?
articles.summary: Fabio Silva stole the show from Harry Kane in Der Klassiker by scoring Borussia Dortmund's late equaliser to secure a 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich. Adam Bate was at the Allianz Arena to see what could prove to be a big moment in the Portugal forward's career
articles.body:
It was magnificent too. The first touch was perfection to protect the ball and give him just enough space to arrow a shot into the far corner with his second. An 89th-minute equaliser away to Bayern Munich to maintain Dortmund's unbeaten record.

There is a feeling within Dortmund that he needed this as a reward for his efforts. Speaking to goalkeeper Gregor Kobel afterwards, he made the point that forwards need goals to feel good. Stealing the show from Kane could be a transformative moment.

Silva's potential has long been debated. He was just 18 when Wolves committed £30m to sign him from Porto, the club's chairman talking of a generational talent. Nominated for the Golden Boy award, this was the very definition of the precocious wonderkid.

But thrust into Premier League action before he was ready proved a struggle. Sixty-two appearances in the competition yielded only four goals, with mixed fortunes on loan at Anderlecht, PSV and Rangers before more promising signs at Las Palmas in LaLiga.

When he finally left Wolves to sign permanently for Dortmund last year, Silva added a seventh different European league to his ledger. But after a first Bundesliga season in which he was largely relegated to the bench, an eighth looked likely in the summer.

Speaking to Silva in August after he scored in the German Super Cup against Bayern, he did not rule out a departure from Dortmund. "I don't know what is going to happen," he said. "Of course, I want to start more games, I want to be more important to this team."

When those comments were put to Silva on Saturday, he acknowledged that there was some uncertainty. "Of course, in the transfer window there were too many noises around me, but this is normal, it is part of football." A conversation changed things.

"I sat with the coach, with the sporting director, and we had an amazing talk before the market closed." Reassured of his role and the chance of an impact at one of Europe's best-supported clubs, he then scored in his first two Bundesliga games of the season.

But opportunities continue to be limited. His only Bundesliga start in the past six weeks came against Eintracht Frankfurt when he was substituted before Maxi Beier's late winner. But this goal feels like a big moment and there are reasons for Silva, now 24, to believe it.

Once regarded as a penalty-box poacher, he has added more to his game as his physicality has developed. He regards himself as a cross between a No 9 and a No 10 and that opens up possibilities alongside the experienced striker Serhou Guirassy.

Silva deputised for him for much of last season, starting only four games together all campaign. While many Dortmund supporters favoured Silva's work rate, his total of three goals compared to Guirassy's 22 reflected his team-mate's greater goal threat.

They have had three starts together this season - Dortmund winning the lot - and Guirassy stayed on the pitch with Silva in Munich having already scored the game's first equaliser. Silva is understandably keen to stress that he can be a partner to Guirassy not his back-up.

"When I am with Serhou on the pitch, I think us together we combine very good. I know Serhou is one of the best players in the world in his position, and I learn with him every day, but everyone can see sometimes we can play together and enjoy playing together."

Frustrations remain. "I prefer to start than to be on the bench. If I say the opposite I am not being 100 per cent honest. But I always try to be positive during the week when I see I don't play. Of course, the first moments I am angry, but after I try to always be positive."

He added: "Because I know that I can be important for the team. Everyone can see this season I am being important if I start on the bench or if I start on the pitch, and I am focused on that because I think we have an amazing squad to fight for good things."

The result in Munich underlined that. It remains in Silva's interests to talk up his ability to play with Guirassy. "I do more than score goals." But this one against Bayern could be huge for him. "I have this feeling," he concluded. "I have more things to give to this club."

articles.title: "Si hay un penalti favorecido al Barcelona no se monta semejante debate nacional"
articles.standfirst: La polémica arbitral divide a La Tribu tras el penalti que Munuera Montero señaló a favor del Real Madrid en su partido contra el Racing de Santander
articles.summary: La polémica arbitral divide a La Tribu tras el penalti que Munuera Montero señaló a favor del Real Madrid en su partido contra el Racing de Santander
articles.body: Emilio Pérez de Rozas, José Luis Allegue, Javier Amaro, Pilar Losantos, María José Hostalrich, Paul Tenorio y Ricardo Rosety han sido los tertulianos de este lunes en La Tribu de Radio MARCA, patrocinada por Sportium durante esta temporada, apara analizar la actualidad deportiva marcada por toda la polémica arbitral de este fin de semana. La polémica por el penalti favorable al Real Madrid ha protagonizado buena parte del debate. Pilar Losantos ha defendido que existen argumentos para señalar la pena máxima, aunque reconoce que la acción admite diferentes interpretaciones. "Es cierto que hay contacto en el estómago y eso es indiscutible", ha asegurado. La tertuliana ha comparado la jugada con otras decisiones arbitrales que, a su juicio, no provocaron la misma repercusión. "Creo que ha habido otros penaltis como por ejemplo el de Lamine contra el Levante, con Mandy, que era infinitamente más escandaloso y no se montó semejante debate nacional", ha señalado. Además, ha criticado la diferencia de criterio que considera que existe cuando las decisiones favorecen al conjunto blanco o al Barcelona. Los Santos ha insistido en que la discusión debe centrarse en la intensidad del contacto y su influencia en la acción. "Creo que es razonable poder plantear que el contacto era lo suficientemente fuerte como para poder decirlo. Y entiendo que es debatible, pero no me parece tan escandaloso", ha explicado. Una interpretación que no comparte María José Hostalrich, que ha sido tajante sobre lo sucedido: "Es que no todos los contactos son penalti. Es que en el fútbol puede haber contacto". La tertuliana ha insistido en la necesidad de diferenciar entre una acción en la que existe contacto y otra que realmente merece ser sancionada: "No todos los contactos dentro del área son penalti". Por su parte, Ricardo Rosety ha puesto el foco en la reacción del futbolista tras el contacto. "Hasta las leyes de la física te dicen que si te ponen un brazo delante, a lo mejor caes para atrás, no caes hacia delante", ha argumentado durante el debate. Raúl Varela ha recordado que José Mourinho había anunciado que reconocería públicamente las decisiones arbitrales que beneficiasen a su equipo. "Ayer lo que cantó un poco fue que Mourinho no salió al paso, que había anunciado que cuando se sintiese beneficiado lo iba a decir", ha apuntado Varela.

articles.summary: El presentador de Despierta San Francisco carga en La Tribu contra la actuación arbitral en Santander
articles.body: David Sánchez ha analizado en La Tribu de Radio MARCA la victoria del Real Madrid ante el Racing de Santander, un encuentro marcado por la polémica arbitral. El periodista ha cargado contra el penalti señalado a favor del conjunto blanco y ha criticado el diferente tratamiento que, a su juicio, reciben las decisiones arbitrales dependiendo del equipo beneficiado. "Escandaloso penalti que le pitan al Real Madrid para abrir el camino de la victoria en Santander ante el Racing", ha comenzado David Sánchez, que, pese a reconocer el buen encuentro del equipo de José Mourinho, ha insistido en la importancia de la decisión arbitral: "En un muy buen partido del equipo de José Mourinho, que no debe de esconder que gracias al árbitro empezaron a conquistar los tres puntos". El periodista ha cuestionado la reacción del entorno madridista cuando las decisiones arbitrales favorecen al equipo blanco. "Porque suele pasar que cuando al Madrid le benefician, que es muchas veces en un año, solo les apetece hablar de fútbol, de dibujos, de sistemas, de bloque alto, de bloque bajo, de Diomandé, de Bellingham, de lo que sea con tal de no reconocer lo evidente", ha asegurado. David Sánchez ha insistido en el papel que, en su opinión, tuvo el colegiado en el desarrollo del encuentro. "Ayer, gracias a Munuera, empezaron a conquistar Santander y a sumar tres puntos importantísimos para seguir a la caza del Barcelona", ha señalado antes de lanzar una advertencia: "Pero que no os engañen, al Madrid ayer le ayudaron". El periodista también ha criticado que las habituales acusaciones sobre el arbitraje y el Barcelona desaparezcan cuando el beneficiado es el Real Madrid. "Se equivocaron, digo los árbitros, y le beneficiaron. Y por eso hoy nadie habla de mugrienta liga de Negreira ni de que el CTA solo ayuda al Barcelona", ha afirmado. Para terminar, David Sánchez ha resumido su indignación con una frase contundente: "Ayer beneficiaron al Madrid y todo el mundo chitón. Solo hablar de fútbol".

articles.title: Sale a la luz el audio del VAR de la mano de Tchouaméni: "Entendemos que es un play the ball..."
articles.standfirst: La RFEF publicó la conversación entre Munuera Montero y Milla Alvendiz que explica por qué el colegiado rectificó su decisión y anuló el penalti
articles.summary: La RFEF publicó la conversación entre Munuera Montero y Milla Alvendiz que explica por qué el colegiado rectificó su decisión y anuló el penalti
articles.body: El penalti señalado a favor del Racing por una supuesta mano de Tchouaméni terminó siendo anulado tras la intervención del VAR. Horas después del encuentro, la RFEF hizo público el audio de la conversación entre Munuera Montero, árbitro principal, y Milla Alvendiz, responsable del VAR, en la que ambos explican los motivos de la decisión. La acción generó numerosas protestas por parte de los jugadores y aficionados del conjunto cántabro. En un primer momento, Munuera Montero señaló el punto de penalti después de recibir el aviso de su asistente. Sin embargo, desde la sala VOR consideraron que existían motivos suficientes para revisar la jugada. "José Luis, te recomiendo una revisión para que valores la cancelación del penalti que has señalado", le comunicaron al colegiado del encuentro. Una vez frente a la pantalla, Munuera Montero pidió diferentes repeticiones para observar cómo se había producido el contacto. "Nosotros observamos que el jugador del Real Madrid, Tchouaméni, juega el balón voluntariamente primero y luego posteriormente le da en la mano. Por lo tanto, entendemos que es un play the ball", explicó Milla Alvendiz. El concepto de 'play de ball' se da cuando un jugador defensivo golpea, despeja o pasa el balón de forma voluntaria y este le rebota o le toca accidentalmente en la mano/brazo en una posición natural. No se considera infracción y el juego debe continuar. Tras revisar las imágenes, llegó a la misma conclusión que sus compañeros de la sala VOR. "Entendemos que en ningún momento el jugador del Racing toca el balón. Al tocar solamente el jugador del Real Madrid y jugar el balón hacia su mano, entendemos que no es penalti", explicó Munuera Montero.

articles.title: Man Utd will be in Premier League relegation zone in December says Paul Merson as Michael Carrick's side hit by poor recruitment
articles.summary: Paul Merson on Manchester United's upcoming prospects, why Lisandro Martinez would not have played for club again under Sir Alex Ferguson and how poor defensive recruitment has left them trying to 'build a house on a puddle'
articles.body:
United were beaten 2-0 at Chelsea on Saturday as they dropped to fourth-bottom of the Premier League, having gone almost two months without a win in all competitions and beating only Ipswich in the league this season.

Goal difference is all which currently separates them from the relegation zone ahead of Crystal Palace - but Merson believes things will get worse before they get better for Carrick and his side.

'Man Utd will be in bottom three in a month'

The first half at Chelsea was alright and then they shot themselves in the foot. What can Michael Carrick do about that? It doesn't matter who's sat on the bench, you could have Carlo Ancelotti, Arsene Wenger, Jose Mourinho and Sir Alex Ferguson in the dugout, and you're not winning a football match.

The problem is the fans love Carrick. The people above, if they're making decisions, they've got to be careful. Then the fans go against them - they can see it's not really Carrick, is it?

Do the people making the decisions upstairs want the fans to turn on them? When that happens, they'll have to go because they'll be under scrutiny. They're not at the moment, because they're keeping the manager.

On December 5, they play Coventry. I'd be shocked if they're not in the bottom three by then. That'll be about a third of the season gone then. They might go and get a big result, Villa looked beatable the other day.

I don't see them getting relegated, absolutely not. But this is not Manchester United.

'Martinez would have never played again under Fergie'

The problem they have at the moment is they're just up against it in a situation where it's out of the manager's hands.

These players earn so much money, some of them will just go out and do and say what they want. They don't get punished, they're just playing the game.

When Lisandro Martinez then goes and gets sent off like that, if it was under Ferguson he'd never play for them again. But they haven't got a squad.

There's no quick fix. They got it all wrong upstairs. The first window, they went for the forward line but it wasn't good enough. Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo, Benjamin Sesko, they're nice players but they're not 20-25 goal-a-season players.

You've got to be a seven, seven and a half out of 10 every week at Manchester United. But they're a four one week, a nine the next. You can play for Wolves or Brentford and do that, no disrespect. The day you're a nine you win the match and everyone's pleased. When you're a four, people say that's just the way it is.

'Where's the balance? You can't build a house on a puddle'

The midfield they bought - I'd love to see what they saw paying £50m for Andre Santos. Tell me what you saw that I didn't when I was watching him every week at Chelsea.

Youri Tielemans, he's a good player but there's no legs around him in the team. He had legs around him when he was playing at Villa.

And then Carlos Baleba's been asked to come into a team that's not very good and be the saviour. He's a kid who played at Brighton, the way that they play, and if they won, they won and if they lost, they lost.

If Brighton had gone to Manchester City on Saturday and got beaten 4-0, no-one would have said a dickie bird. And Manchester United lose at Chelsea, they're fourth-bottom, and everyone's going mad. He must be thinking, 'oh my God'. I like him but he needs time.

How do I know there's no balance in the midfield they've bought and they don't? Two years ago, you're looking at Casemiro and saying he's a million miles off it. Now you look at it and think they miss him.

And now they say they'll work on the defence in the next window. It's madness - you can't build a house on a puddle. You just can't. Why not start with the defence first and then go from there?

They say they're going to go and outscore teams but they haven't bought players who score enough goals.

I don't know where everyone expects them to be. I didn't expect them to beat Como, I didn't expect them to beat Bournemouth, I didn't expect them to beat Chelsea and I don't expect them to beat Villa.

Analysis: When will Man Utd's winless run end?

Manchester United have not recorded a victory for nine matches across all competitions, failing to keep a clean sheet during that entire run.

The last time United went 10 matches without a win was in 1984 and it has only ever happened six times in the club's history.

As things stand, this side are still some way off equalling the club's longest winless run, which was 16 matches in 1930.

But United's only wins this season have come against Ipswich Town and Sabah and they face a daunting run of fixtures coming up.

In football things can change quickly, but, as Merson points out, on current form it is hard to see where United's next win might come from.

articles.title: Maurizio Mariani arbitrará el duelo ante el AEK de Atenas
articles.standfirst: El colegiado italiano dirigirá por cuarta vez al Real Madrid en la Champions, donde presenta un balance de dos victorias y una derrota
articles.summary: El colegiado italiano dirigirá por cuarta vez al Real Madrid en la Champions, donde presenta un balance de dos victorias y una derrota
articles.body: Maurizio Mariani (Roma, 1982) será el encargado de dirigir el AEK de Atenas-Real Madrid de este miércoles. El colegiado italiano, de 44 años, es uno de los árbitros habituales de la Serie A y forma parte de la categoría Élite de la UEFA desde 2024. Internacional desde 2019, ha ido ganando peso en el panorama arbitral europeo hasta convertirse en uno de los representantes italianos en las grandes citas del fútbol internacional. El encuentro de Atenas será el cuarto que Mariani arbitre al Real Madrid en la Champions. Su primer precedente se remonta a septiembre de 2022, cuando dirigió el triunfo blanco ante el Leipzig en el Santiago Bernabéu (2-0), en la fase de grupos. Dos años después volvió a cruzarse en el camino madridista, aunque con un desenlace diferente: el Lille se impuso por 1-0 en Francia, en un encuentro en el que mostró cinco tarjetas amarillas a jugadores del equipo español. El último precedente es mucho más reciente y tiene un recuerdo especialmente positivo para el madridismo. Mariani fue el árbitro de la ida de los octavos de final de la Champions 2025/26 entre el Real Madrid y el Manchester City, resuelta con un contundente 3-0 en el Bernabéu. De esta forma, el balance del equipo blanco con el italiano es de dos victorias y una derrota, con cinco goles a favor y uno en contra. Mariani también cuenta con experiencia en grandes finales. En 2025 dirigió tanto la final de la Coppa Italia entre el Milan y el Bolonia, que terminó con triunfo boloñés (0-1), como la del Mundial sub-20 de Chile, en la que Marruecos derrotó a Argentina (2-0). En mayo de 2026 fue designado para dirigir la final de la Conference League entre el Crystal Palace y el Rayo Vallecano, otro reconocimiento a su trayectoria internacional.

articles.title: B/R's 2026 College Football Playoff Bracket Projections and Predictions After Week 9
articles.summary: Outside of Ohio State's loss at USC, Week 9 was largely about survival for the highest-ranked college football teams.
articles.body:
Outside of Ohio State's loss at USC, Week 9 was largely about survival for the highest-ranked college football teams.

Notre Dame struggled early before pulling away from Navy. Minnesota put a scare into Indiana, but the reigning national champs found a way to win in overtime. Miami walked out of North Carolina with an uncomfortable victory, as well.

Most importantly, though, they all avoided a loss.

But the pressure to win is only increasing. The first edition of the 2026 College Football Playoff rankings will be unveiled on Tuesday, Nov. 3, and the Week 10 slate is packed full of headline-worthy games.

The projected bracket is a reflection of B/R's Top 25 dropped into the organization of the official CFP format.

After a surprising loss at Cincinnati, Texas Tech benched Will Hammond in favor of Thomas Castellanos. His mobility provided the offense with a new element, and the Red Raiders racked up 328 yards on the ground. Castellanos—who also threw for 144 yards and two scores—scampered for 117 yards and a touchdown as J'Koby Williams notched a career-best 175 rushing yards.

Steve Angeli returned last weekend and propelled Syracuse to an overtime triumph at North Carolina. For an encore, Angeli's last-minute touchdown pass to Noah Meyers allowed Cuse to stun 19th-ranked SMU. The result put a major dent in SMU's hopes of a second CFP trip in three seasons, although the 6-2 Mustangs aren't completely out of the conversation just yet.

In the first game without QB Julian Sayin, Ohio State stumbled. Prior to halftime, all three drives that reached USC's 25-yard line ended with a field goal. Add in a fumble near USC's 30 during the third quarter, and it's no surprise the Buckeyes had fallen into a 27-9 hole. Ohio State has zero margin for error left in its CFP pursuit.

1. Miami 2. Georgia 3. Utah 4. Indiana 5. UCLA 6. BYU 7. Notre Dame 8. Kentucky 9. LSU 10. Tennessee 11. Alabama 12. Texas 13. Ohio State 14. Texas Tech 15. Ole Miss 16. Wake Forest 17. Boise State 18. USC 19. Houston 20. Iowa 21. Arizona 22. Missouri 23. South Carolina 24. UTSA 25. New Mexico

Seeding is a reflection of how B/R's Top 25 would shape the bracket.

Power 4 Champions and Top Group of 6 Team

In all likelihood, Miami will be ranked No. 1 when the College Football Playoff rankings are unveiled on Tuesday night. Georgia and Utah, in some order, should be second and third, as well.

Beyond that, it gets rather interesting.

Remember last season, when the selection committee kept Notre Dame above Miami despite the latter's head-to-head win until the bitter end, making for a fully avoidable controversy? Will the 7-1 Fighting Irish be ranked ahead of 7-1 BYU despite losing the recent matchup in Provo?

How about the SEC, which is a lovely disaster? Kentucky lost to Alabama but defeated LSU. Alabama beat Kentucky but lost to Tennessee. Texas has quality wins over Ohio State, Tennessee and Ole Miss but also fell to Oklahoma and Florida. Ole Miss toppled LSU but dropped games at UF and Texas.

In the latter half of the ranking, we'll be tracking which Group of Six programs crack the poll. Boise State, New Mexico and UTSA are prime candidates.

Don't get terribly hung up about a specific order. We have a month remaining in the regular season, and changes are inevitable.

Still, this is a valuable first look at the committee's early perceptions.

Although it's an atrocious kickoff time locally—10 a.m., seriously—the Holy War is a stellar way to open Saturday's action. BYU owns a three-game winning streak in the series, but Utah is unbeaten in 2026 and playing at home. This should be a massively important result in the Big 12 standings.

What a day in the SEC, huh? Within the league, two programs—Kentucky and Georgia—have exactly one conference loss. The six teams with a pair of SEC setbacks, wildly enough, are everyone else in this group. Essentially, that means the eight schools with legitimate SEC aspirations are in action opposite each other. It's safe to say we'll have a few takeaways on Saturday.

Sharing the prime-time spotlight with Georgia and Ole Miss, top-ranked Miami travels north to Notre Dame. Last season, Miami pulled out a 27-24 victory that ultimately pushed ND to the wrong side of the CFP bubble. As if a top-10 showdown weren't important enough, there are plenty of emotions here, too.

articles.title: Ohio State's Season Is Over and 8 Overreactions After Week 9 of 2026 College Football Season
articles.summary: If pandemonium is what you seek, college football is the sport for you.
articles.body:
If pandemonium is what you seek, college football is the sport for you.

There were upsets. There were near-upsets. There were shocking losses. There were enormous moments that will have an impact on coaches' jobs, the College Football Playoff and beyond.

For the third consecutive week, the No. 2-ranked team lost. In many respects, that sums up the current nature of the sport: unpredictable, volatile, delightful.

It also makes the prospects of generating overreactions awfully easy. With plenty of material to work with, let's overreact to what we saw—which was plenty—once again.

DJ Lagway Will Still Be a Football Star...for Someone

To say it's been an up-and-down few seasons for the former 5-star quarterback would be an understatement.

He began his career at Florida and showed flashes of brilliance as a freshman. As a sophomore, he struggled mightily with turnovers and then decided to head to Baylor over the offseason, choosing the Bears over other higher profile programs.

This year, Lagway has produced more flashes. And on Friday night against UCF, all of the talent—the size, the mobility and the arm—was on display. The Bears clobbered the Knights 41-9, thanks in large part to his four-touchdown performance.

The fact that Lagway has played at multiple programs that have fired head coaches certainly hasn't aided his development. Still, at 6'3" and nearly 240 pounds, the QB has the build NFL teams are in constant search of.

And then there's the arm. No one in college football throws a better football, and that isn't up for debate. Whether he's playing for Baylor, an NFL team or another college football program in 2027, the ceiling is still enormous, and the best is yet to come.

Sure, we're in the business of overreactions, but this one feels appropriate.

Playing its first game without starting quarterback Julian Sayin, Ohio State lost to USC 30-18, although it never felt that close.

Quarterback Luke Fahey posted decent numbers, throwing the ball 38 times, but the offense clearly wasn't the same despite gaining more than 460 yards.

The offensive line didn't help matters, and neither did the 11 penalties. We can look at QBs if we want, but this was largely a mess all around.

As for what it means, it's hard not to overreact. Sayin will be out for at least the regular season—and perhaps longer—which puts this team in a bind. The Buckeyes still have games against Oregon, Northwestern, Nebraska and Michigan, and it feels likely that an additional loss is still coming.

A third loss would all but take Ohio State out of playoff consideration. But even if they somehow make it through, the ceiling on this team feels clear. Whether that next loss comes in the regular season or beyond, it's coming soon enough.

The Heisman Race Just Became Wildly Interesting

One of the many impacts of Ohio State's loss is the fact that wideout Jeremiah Smith is no longer the favorite to win the Heisman, according to FanDuel.

Smith has been the favorite for the better part of the season, and he still caught 10 passes for 83 yards and a touchdown in his team's defeat. Still, it's clear the passing offense will likely be limited without Sayin, and that changes the entire outlook of the sport's most prestigious award.

As such, suddenly things seem incredibly wide open. Clarity, however, is coming.

Miami quarterback Darian Mensah is now the favorite, and his favorite target, wide receiver Malachi Toney, isn't far behind. Right behind him are Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr and Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss.

As for that clarity, look no further than Week 10. Notre Dame will play Miami, and the winner of that game, depending on how things shake out, will impact this race in a major way.

Elsewhere, Ole Miss will take on Georgia in primetime, providing Chambliss with a gigantic spotlight to play his way back into the discussion.

Where will the Heisman moments come from? We shall see. But with a seismic lineup of games on deck, a shakeup is coming soon enough.

Georgia Is the Best Team in College Football...For Now

A few weeks later, and it's hard to piece together how exactly this team lost to Auburn.

Regardless, Georgia looked like Georgia while playing Florida on Saturday, suffocating the Gators in all areas. The Bulldogs beat the Gators 27-8, rushing for more than 200 yards while forcing four turnovers on defense.

It was a complete effort, and it was needed after the team lost as a massive favorite a few weeks ago. It was also a critical performance given the timing. Georgia plays two of its next three games on the road—at Ole Miss and at South Carolina. In between, the Bulldogs take on a very capable Missouri squad.

While there are more explosive offenses around the country, Georgia has all the pieces.

At quarterback, Gunner Stockton, who wasn't asked to do much on Saturday, is still dependable. On defense, the Bulldogs have future NFL players at every level and a sensational talent in Chris Cole.

Then there's Kirby Smart, who knows how to navigate the ups and downs of a college football season.

The next two weeks will tell us plenty, although we're penciling in Georgia as college football's best team and not thinking twice.

College Football Kickers Have Changed the Sport

There was a time when kicking across college football was unreliable. You remember those days: Even extra points were an adventure, and 35-yard field goals felt like coin flips.

In the final 19 seconds of Indiana's game against Minnesota—a game that was far closer than anyone expected—we saw two 60-yard field goals. That's not a typo.

Minnesota's Luke Drzewiecki was the first to hit a 60-yarder, which gave the Gophers a 16-13 lead. Paddy McAteer then responded with a 60-yard field goal of his own for Indiana, which sent the game into overtime.

The Hoosiers ultimately won the game 23-16 in extra time, prevailing once again in ugly fashion.

As for the kicking, it's hard to find the words. To witness two 60-yard field goals with massive implications in a single game shows how different things are.

By no means is it perfect. We still see plenty of wayward kicks every now and then. But kicking across the sport has improved dramatically in the past five years, and we just witnessed how it is changing the way these games are decided.

"Bad" feels a tad too harsh and "inconsistent" seems to miss the mark.

Instead, we're declaring the Nebraska football program cursed, because it's hard to describe what we're seeing at this point.

With Nebraska leading 7–3, Washington faced fourth-and-18 with less than two minutes remaining. A stop would have all but ended the game, but the Cornhuskers allowed a 24-yard completion and a 25-yard touchdown two plays later.

The next drive, Anthony Colandrea threw an interception, which Washington returned for a touchdown. Just like that, Nebraska lost 17-10 at home, despite being more than a touchdown favorite.

Matt Rhule's team has now lost its last three games by a combined 13 points. And if that sounds familiar, that's because it is.

Since 2014, Nebraska has lost 51 one-score games, which is 12 more than any team in college football. It doesn't matter who the coach or the quarterback is; the theme has stayed consistent for more than a decade.

There's a reason we haven't talked about the Utes much this season. The strength of schedule early on was, well, lackluster.

Over the past few weeks, however, the Utes have showcased incredible balance. Utah's defense dominated in Week 8, and its offense blew the doors off Cincinnati in Week 9.

Yes, it was Cincinnati. But Utah clobbered the Bearcats 49-25, racking up 536 yards of offense along the way.

Quarterback Devon Dampier was electric, throwing for three touchdowns. Given how talented he is as a runner, it was refreshing to see the team's passing offense rule the day.

As the Big 12 has seen its top teams suffer loss after loss, Utah hasn't budged. Still unbeaten, the Utes will play rival BYU in Utah's biggest game of the season. A week later, this group will travel to Arizona, which won't be easy.

While there is still a lot to be decided, there's also a lot to like. Utah has played its way into the playoff conversation, and the team has all the major pieces to be a problem against every opponent moving forward.

The College Football Playoff Rankings Mean Nothing Until the Very End

Maybe this is more of a rant than an overreaction, but we're letting it fly regardless.

On Tuesday night, the first College Football Playoff Rankings will be revealed. It will be the first of five Tuesdays before the field is finalized the day after most conference championship games are played.

As a reminder, this is all in good fun. It's a way to draw attention to the postseason, which will be decided next month. It's a way to engage—and enrage—fan bases throughout college football's home stretch.

It's also, if we're being honest, pretty meaningless.

With a massive Week 10 on the horizon, the rankings that will be revealed on Tuesday will be torn to pieces only four days later. It doesn't matter how those games go; change is coming regardless.

That's not to say you shouldn't watch. The show, if nothing else, is wildly entertaining. Seeing the way the committee thinks about college football—especially in the midst of such a wild season—will be revealing.

This show was constructed to generate conversation, and it will do just that.

But the first Top 25 won't tell us anything at all. Thankfully, we have so much meaningful football still to play. The only constant over the next month will be change.

articles.title: Ranking the Potential Top 10 2027 Free Transfers in World Football
articles.summary: January is an important time in football. For those whose contracts expire in the summer of 2027, it's the moment when pre-agreements can be made with other clubs.
articles.body:
January is an important time in football. For those whose contracts expire in the summer of 2027, it's the moment when pre-agreements can be made with other clubs.

That's a worrying prospect for teams that have star players moving into the final months of their deals. Right now, some truly world-class names could be available.

Let's take a look at the most intriguing.

Note: Harry Kane, Thibaut Courtois, and others are reportedly very close to signing extensions, so they have been omitted .

It wasn't long ago that Kaoru Mitoma was linked with plenty of big-money moves away from Brighton.

The Japanese winger had an excellent 2024-25 season, scoring 10 goals and providing four assists in 28 Premier League starts and eight substitute appearances. His directness is a breath of fresh air.

However, persistent injuries on either side of that season have tempered the hype considerably. Mitoma missed 31 games the year before through injury, most of which came after a serious back issue. He sat out of 33 matches in 25-26, with a persistent hamstring problem keeping him out for more than half a year.

Brighton have quietly moved on under Fabian Hürzeler, who has been unable to call on the talented 29-year-old this season. Plenty of clubs could be interested if Mitoma becomes available, although his injury history may affect the terms they are willing to offer.

Hakan Çalhanoğlu is approaching the end of his contract with Inter Milan and has yet to agree to a further extension.

The Turkish international, 32, is a mainstay at the San Siro, having impressed since joining in 2021. Inter has good reason to keep him, but his future remains unresolved.

Çalhanoğlu's control and creativity in midfield make him an attractive proposition. He's got a bit of everything: great distribution, plenty of grit, and an eye for goal. There's a leader here if anyone can tempt him away.

Cristiano Ronaldo seems allergic to the word "retirement" right now. Portugal coach Jorge Jesus even tried to provide a slight hint towards his future prospects with a benching that ended up being a story just because it's Ronaldo.

CR7 is contracted with Al-Nassr until June 2027. He is set on reaching 1000 career goals. He's not going to stop until that happens. His profile may still attract one or two clubs to have a pop if he doesn't soon extend with his current side.

In many ways, Lisandro Martínez of Argentina and Lisandro Martínez of Manchester United feel like different players.

The first is a World Cup winner. A leader on a team who fights for every ball and never knows when to quit. He's scrappy, not small .

Then there's the United version, who can be a very good player, but is having an abysmal season, summed up by his ridiculous red card in Saturday's defeat at Chelsea.

Martínez's recent criticism of the United hierarchy was overdue, but it could help push him towards an exit. United hold an option to extend his contract until 2028; if they leave it unused, another team could pick up the 28-year-old for free and give him a better chance to rediscover his form.

A lot of players receive criticism for moving to Saudi Arabia, but João Félix's career has improved massively since he took the leap.

The 26-year-old is now settled, not being passed around struggling European teams without making an impact, and again looks something like the player we all hoped he'd become when he broke through at Benfica.

The conversation has certainly changed around the versatile forward. His increased confidence has led to more than one goal every other game for Al-Nassr.

That kind of form could have European teams circling once more, although Al-Nassr reportedly holds an option to extend his contract until 2029, complicating any prospect of a free transfer next summer.

Not too much brainpower needed here. Alisson remains a top-class goalkeeper, whose quality has probably not been spotlighted as much recently due to Liverpool's overall struggle in the last 18 months.

The goalkeeper market is a pretty difficult one at the moment. Landing Alisson on a free transfer should be considered a smart deal for most teams, as he's still got plenty to offer at 34 years old.

An excellent shot-stopper with quality on the ball, the Brazilian is a rare type at the highest level.

Yasin Ayari is something of an outlier on this list because he isn't a million years old. The 23-year-old Swede is benefiting from some excellent developmental time with Brighton, a side that has impressed more than any other in the Premier League this season.

His well-roundedness makes him an interesting prospect who is destined to end up at an elite club. He can dribble, score goals, and work hard in a system that forces everyone to take responsibility. His winning goal against Manchester City on Saturday will only add to the attention he's receiving.

Ayari may well turn out to be the best-value free signing on this list, but Brighton reportedly hold an option to extend his contract until 2028. They would have to leave that option unused to risk losing him for nothing—and, to be fair, they rarely drop the ball on contracts.

Granted, Virgil van Dijk will nearly be 36 years old when his contract expires.

It seems unlikely Liverpool will let him walk. He's more than just the captain; he's a figure of the Reds' success and an important pillar of strength at a transitional time for the club. His value exceeds whether or not he's still putting in impactful performances on the pitch.

Van Dijk has worked hard to overcome some bad form in recent years. He's not as fast or as imposing as he used to be, but he could still do a job for most teams.

Somehow, Brahim Díaz is already 27 years old. His career is passing in a flash. At this stage, he's only ever made more than 20 league starts in a single campaign on two occasions. That is absolutely mad for a player of his quality.

Díaz is once again struggling to hold down a starting spot at Real Madrid. The Moroccan is a vital factor for his national team and should be the focal point of a club side, too.

Surely there's a team out there who fancy taking his creative skills and building around them? Seems a no-brainer for free.

This one has been lingering for a while. Bruno Fernandes' relationship with Manchester United is best summed up by breaking the Premier League's single-season assists record one season and being left on the bench after questioning the head coach's tactics the next.

The Red Devils have fought off interest from Saudi Arabia before, but the Portuguese international's recent poor form and questionable behaviour (including liking a social media post about loyalty) may signal the end.

To put it bluntly: Fernandes should be playing for a far better team than Manchester United. He is one of the best creative players of his generation and has the ability to improve any team in the world.

Fernandes and his family are well-established in Manchester, and he has resisted the temptation to leave before. Now might be the time to upend things. United hold an option to extend his contract until 2028, though, so a free departure next summer would depend on them declining to exercise it.

articles.title: Simeone: "Kane le hace muy bien a los niños, deja un legado de que se puede llegar a su lugar trabajando"
articles.standfirst: El Cholo no dudó en elogiar al flamante Balón de Oro en vísperas de su estreno en el Metropolitano
articles.summary: El Cholo no dudó en elogiar al flamante Balón de Oro en vísperas de su estreno en el Metropolitano
articles.body: Diego Pablo Simeone compareció ante los medios de comunicación junto a Álex Baena para analizar el choque del Atlético y el Bayern. El técnico argentino repasó la actualidad de los suyos antes de medirse al gigante alemán Final en la Champions: "No sé cuánto vamos a seguir en la Champions, pero pero espero que no me hagan esta pregunta en todos los partidos. Para el club es algo maravilloso, pero nosotros vamos partido a partido, este escenario es muy lindo, pero necesitamos trabajar y depender de lo que vamos a hacer cada partido". Sensación: "De todo, me pasan tres situaciones por la cabeza, soy un agradecido por lo conseguido en estos 15 años y lo que estamos viviendo el club, la afición, nosotros... Hay que disfrutarlo y enfrentarlo con entusiasmo e ilusión, nos enfrentamos a un rival muy duro, muy bueno y tendremos que llevar el partido a donde creemos que les podemos hacer daño". Orden o protagonismo: "Me gustaría atacar los 80 minutos y dejarles diez a ellos, hacer un gol de 20 toques como en Levante... pero la realidad es otra, nos encontramos a un equipo potente, fuerte, tendremos que enfrentarnos a momentos difíciles, duros, a poder salir de una presión que trabajan muy bien ...". Kane: "Primero felicitarlo por el Balón de Oro obtenido justamente. Es increíble, siempre me ha gustado, en su maduración con los años ha encontrado mejores lugares sin alejarse del gol. Comprometido para el trabajo, para sacar al equipo de atrás cuando lo necesita, es un hombre gol. Su talento le hace muy bien al fútbol y a los chicos que le miran porque deja un legado de que se puede llegar a un lugar importante trabajando". Qué le ocupa: "Encontrar el equilibrio y la regularidad que es lo más difícil y lo que queremos todos los entrenadores. Vamos a seguir insistiendo en eso". Metropolitano en esta semana: "La semana ya empezó con el Levante, al que ganamos; sigue con el Bayern, donde necesitamos a nuestra gente como suele estar, fuerte y cerca de los futbolistas. Lo que transmiten los jugadores lo siguen y ojalá podamos llevar esa energía que nos traen y disfrutar de lo que nos viene porque son partidos bonitos e importantes". Lookman: "No sé si juega en algún lugar donde no quiere. No empezó como le hubiera gustado, pero la temporada pasada también a Julián le pasó, atravesó un momento difícil y salió. Y Griezmann tuvo un momento que no hacía goles y salió. Lookman es el que tiene más duelos en el último tercio y confío mucho en él, no quiero que entre en la frustración, es parte de la vida y el fútbol. Hasta que un día empiece a hacer gol y a asistir. Esperemos que ese sea el camino que pueda seguir". Obed Vargas. "Está trabajando muy bien, con mucho entusiasmo e ilusión y comprometido con lo que hace. Compite con chicos como Barrios, Koke, Morten o Mendoza que lo hacen muy bien. Hay muchos jugadores y esperamos al día que haga cosas en los entrenamientos que nos lleven a decir 'se merece jugar porque lo está haciendo muy bien'". Piezas que faltan. "Siempre los partidos importantes, especialmente en Champions, son diferentes por la categoría del rival y la exposición que te genera. Tenemos en el medio a Cardoso y Morten fuera, Koke vuelve con ganas pero el partido puede ser largo, Mendoza y Obed, también Llorente... Debemos pensar de aquí a las 6 de la tarde de mañana para decidir".

articles.title: Hansi Flick: "Emery es uno de los mejores técnicos de Europa y del mundo"
articles.standfirst: El preparador desmenuza el cruce continental contra el Aston Villa
articles.summary: El preparador desmenuza el cruce continental contra el Aston Villa
articles.body: Hansi Flick atendió a los medios de comunicación este lunes en la previa de la cuarta jornada de la fase liga de la Champions League, que le cruza con el Aston Villa de Unai Emery. El preparador alemán se deshizo en elogios hacia el técnico vasco y el equipo de la Premier, pero se mostró seguro de la calidad de su plantilla para ganar el encuentro... y la competición continental. Bajas "No hacemos mal las cosas. En el último partido, contra el Alavés, hubo un error. Pero el equipo tuvo confianza. Hace bien las cosas". Christensen "Tenemos que esperar para saber cuándo vuelve. Ayer se entrenó pero sólo hizo de comodín. Hay que ver cómo evoluciona". Balde "Creo que esta situación es normal. Si no juegas, te falta confianza. Pero lo que veo en su caso es que en las sesiones hace bien las cosas. Es una buena opción, pero debo decidir. Joao hizo un gran trabajo, está a un buen nivel. No es fácil. Hay que decidir lo mejor para el equipo. Esto no afecta a una persona o a mí, me centro en el equipo. Hablé con él tras la última rueda de prensa. Respeto mucho a Balde. Es muy joven, es de La Masia... le intento ayudar para que recupere la confianza. Está intentando volver al nivel de antes. Es un gran tipo y un jugador fantástico". Alineación condicionada "Sólo me centro en un partido. Estoy centrado en el encuentro contra el Aston Villa, sólo. Está en un gran momento y Emery es uno de los mejores técnicos de Europa. Tiene muy claro cómo jugar y me encanta lo que veo de él. La Champions es especial en cada partido. Y los rivales son todos complicados. Será un partido difícil". Semana exigente "Sabemos que a este nivel puede pasar cualquier cosa. El resultado contra el Real Madrid podría haber sido diferente. Tenemos confianza. Ganamos 11 partidos seguidos. Os centráis en las dos derrotas. Pero yo confío en mi equipo. Hay que centrarse en el Aston Villa, en la Champions. Queremos estar entre los mejores ocho". Errores en defensa "Tenemos a cuatro jugadores lesionados, si analizas su calidad ves que no es normal gestionar esta situación. No es sencillo. Pero cuando veo a Frenkie que tras lesión te dice que juega de central... e igual Brian. Quien juega, lo hace como un equipo. Tras el parón espero tenerlos a todos de vuelta, incluido Olmo. Espart, tal vez, para el próximo año". Gavi "No lo veo en el lateral derecho. Pero todos conocemos su calidad. Gavi siempre es una opción, pero cuando empieza el partido esa opción puede desaparecer y no siempre puedes seguir tu plan inicial. He hablado con él". Brian Fariñas "Lamine y él son amigos, tienen buena conexión. Lo hicieron muy bien contra el Alavés. Es una opción mañana, pero puede jugar también otro...". Gerard Martín "Puede jugar de central y de lateral izquierdo. Está en nuestros planes que pueda estar en las dos posiciones". Raphinha "No sé mucho de Brasil, no es mi trabajo. Pero aquí está a un nivel espectacular. Sus puntos fuertes son increíbles y se adaptan a nuestro estilo de juego, con y sin balón. Está muy centrado, se adapta al rival, ve espacios en los que atacar... y hay jugadores que hacen el último pase. Está muy centrado. Es nuestro capitán. Demuestra su calidad desde el inicio de curso". Críticas por las derrotas "No me sorprende, es la realidad. Hay que demostrar las cosas. Jugamos nuestro mejor fútbol y no hay excusa. Los resultados podrían ser diferentes. Estamos al mismo nivel que el Real Madrid y el PSG. Pero me centro en los próximos partidos, no miro atrás ni en las derrotas ni en las victorias. Tenemos una calidad enorme para conseguir nuestros objetivos: ganar LaLiga y la Champions. Estoy seguro de que tenemos la calidad y podemos escribir la historia. Las derrotas no han cambiado nada. Para vosotros, en el fútbol, es normal centrarse en las derrotas, es más interesante". Emery "Es uno de los mejores técnicos de Europa y tal vez del mundo. Con muchos éxitos. Y su equipo juega con una estructura clara, en defensa y ataque. Lo tiene todo muy claro. Es increíble ver a un equipo como el suyo, su confianza con el balón... Jackson está a un nivel increíble. Será un partido difícil contra un buen equipo y un buen entrenador".

articles.title: Flick ofrece el pesimista parte médico de los lesionados del Barça
articles.standfirst: No recupera a ningún futbolista para los próximos partidos
articles.summary: No recupera a ningún futbolista para los próximos partidos
articles.body: El Barcelona no recuperará a ningún lesionado para el cruce de mañana martes contra el Aston Villa, de la cuarta jornada de la fase liga de la Champions League. Andreas Christensen, tampoco estará disponible a pesar de que había ciertas esperanzas. Esta mañana, Hansi Flick ofreció el parte médico de los jugadores que hay en la enfermería y las informaciones no son muy positivas. El técnico germano, el club y los futbolistas prefieren no correr riesgos y su regreso será tan prudente como seguro. Andreas Christensen hizo ayer domingo una pequeña parte del trabajo con el grupo. Pero fue mínimo. De hecho, sólo saltó al terreno de juego para hacer de comodín. Se sumó al equipo de forma muy puntual, y esta mañana no saltó al césped. Se quedó haciendo ejercicios individuales: sigue con la rehabilitación de la lesión muscular en el recto anterior del cuádriceps izquierdo que sufrió a finales de septiembre. No estará contra el Aston Villa y tampoco se le espera para el cruce del domingo contra el Atlético de Madrid. De hecho, Flick cree que el exprofesional del Chelsea no regresará hasta después del descanso por los partidos internacionales. Como la mayoría de los lesionados. "Tras el parón espero tenerlos a todos de vuelta, incluido Olmo. Espart, tal vez, para el próximo año", dijo, resignado, el preparador azulgrana. Por lo tanto, Jules Koundé tampoco estará contra los de Simeone en el cruce en el Metropolitano del próximo fin de semana, a pesar de que incluso se le esperaba para la pasada jornada: no estaba descartado contra el Alavés. También Eric García retornará tras los partidos de selecciones, como Dani Olmo. Más tiempo necesitará, en cambio, Xavi Espart, que padece una lesión en el tobillo derecho y al que no espera hasta 2027. Por otro lado, Roony, que se está recuperando de una rotura del ligamento cruzado de la rodilla derecha, no tiene aún fecha de retorno.

articles.title: Tres analistas vieron penalti y dos no
articles.standfirst: Los ex árbitros que juzgan las actuaciones de los actuales colegiados en las principales emisoras de radio no se pudieron de acuerdo en la jugada entre Nico y Aramburu
articles.summary: Los ex árbitros que juzgan las actuaciones de los actuales colegiados en las principales emisoras de radio no se pudieron de acuerdo en la jugada entre Nico y Aramburu
articles.body: La acción en la que Alejandro Hernández Hernández señaló penalti de Jon Mikel Aramburu sobre Nico Williams, que transformado por Berenguer termimó siendo clave para la victoria del Athletic de Bilbao sobre la Real Sociedad en el derbi de San Mamés, generó mucha polémica en el campo y también fuera de el. Tres analistas arbitrales de las principales radios vieron pena máxima, mientras que dos no. Pablo González Fuertes, en el ‘Marcador’ de Radio MARCA, opinó así de la acción, no sin antes dudar. “Hay dos repeticiones en las que parece que hay penalti pero, vista la última repetición toca balón, luego no sería penalti, porque el toque de balón sería antes que a Nico y el balón cambia de trayectoria”. Pedro Martín, en la Cope, fue tajante. “Aramburu toca la pelota claramente, es una de las jugadas más escandalosas de no ir al VAR. Es un error escandaloso, para esto está el VAR, para corregir esos errores y estos dos árbitros eran los españoles en el Mundial”. Andujar Oliver, en Onda Cero, estuvo en la misma línea. “Toca balón Aramburu, no es penalti en absoluto. Tiene que ir al VAR, Del Cerro tiene que decirle que vaya a ver la jugada y que rectifique”. Iturralde González, en la SER, lo tuvo muy claro. “Es penalti, Nico toca la bola, Aramburu no toca balón, aunque es muy dificilísimo diferenciarlo”. Alfonso Pino Zamorano, en RNE, es el otro analista que vio pena máxima. “Alejandro está de frente, lo ve muy claro, para mí penalti, se lleva la pierna izquierda”.

articles.title: To dive or not to dive? Football's big dilemma after Alexander Isak non-penalty
articles.summary: Liverpool feel Alexander Isak should have been awarded a penalty against Arsenal but with the striker not appealing for the decision and the VAR staying out of it, should he have made more of it?
articles.body:
Bradley Barcola delivered a cross into the Arsenal penalty area, with Liverpool striker Alexander Isak seemingly ready to nod home an equaliser.

The Sweden international just failed to get his head on the ball, and it drifted out of play.

Isak simply turned around to make his way back up the field in readiness for the goal-kick.

Replays showed that Jurrien Timber had a handful of Isak's shirt. Surely that prevented the striker from being able to play the ball?

Yet Isak did not complain. Without watching those replays you would have no inkling there was a potential penalty.

Referee Andy Madley did not see anything. The video assistant referee (VAR), Stuart Attwell, decided there was not enough in it for a review.

"There is a clear grab of the shirt," Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola said after the 1-0 defeat by the Gunners at Anfield on Sunday.

"The answer is you have to dive, if you don't dive they won't call it."

When players do dive, they get criticised.

Take Alexis Mac Allister, described as "embarrassing" by Jamie Carragher for throwing himself to the ground, claiming he was headbutted by Noni Madueke in the second half.

You can understand Iraola's frustrations at not getting the penalty, so why did the VAR not get involved?

And do players really have to dive to get decisions?

Holding is all about the impact on an opponent

Cast your mind back to a game between Sunderland and Fulham in February.

Harry Wilson swings a free-kick into the penalty area. The ball flies through to Sunderland goalkeeper Robin Roefs, who punches it to safety.

But on the ground is Calvin Bassey, who immediately gets up and appeals to referee Craig Pawson, arms outstretched. The Fulham player wants a spot-kick for a shirt pull by Brian Brobbey.

Nothing is picked up on-field but the VAR, Tony Harrington, identifies a tug on the shirt and sends the referee to the monitor to give a penalty.

There are striking similarities to Timber on Isak.

One resulted in a VAR penalty, but the other did not.

One player went to ground, but the other did not.

Rather than to dive, perhaps there is a better description of what Isak had to do: give the referee and the VAR a decision to make.

" Arsenal got lucky," Danny Murphy said on Match of the Day. "If Isak maybe makes a bit more of it. I hate to see players exaggerate, but he's going to score. It's a big moment in the game."

Shirt pulling is not in itself an automatic foul. The determination is always about how it affects the opponent.

As the law says: "A holding offence occurs only when a player's contact with an opponent's body or equipment impedes the opponent's movement."

Indeed, the 'coat hanger effect', when a player's shirt is pulled well away from the body, is more likely to be penalised.

Still, impact is crucial. And if Isak gives the impression there has been no impact, that is going to be a factor.

Former Premier League assistant referee Darren Cann told BBC Sport: "It has to be sustained holding - some will say it was sustained, some will say it wasn't. But it's interesting that Isak didn't even appeal."

There is some annoyance in refereeing circles that the goalposts keep being moved when analysing decisions.

One moment video officials are being told that the VAR should not use slow-motion replays. And then, as was the case with Isak, slow-motion replays are used as the case for the prosecution.

There seems to be far less in the incident at full speed, that the hold of the shirt is more fleeting with minimal impact.

With the high bar for intervention this season, this may go down as an on-field error but not to the threshold for a VAR intervention.

"If he goes to the floor, they call the penalty 100%," Iraola said. "It shouldn't be like this but it is what it is."

The Spaniard's comments are largely true, of course, as we saw with Bassey. But that is not always the case, especially this season.

In the summer, Uefa referees' chief Roberto Rosetti said that there were "too many reviews", which had led to attempts to play for or earn video decisions.

There is now a greater focus on players who dive or embellish contact to 'win' penalties.

The number of interventions in the Premier League has historically been the lowest in Europe, which is probably why the number of subjective reviews (14) is exactly the same as last season after nine rounds.

And with the high bar, a small amount of contact with no appeal is unlikely to lead to a review.

The flipside is why players should have to appeal? After all, this is not cricket. And we've seen plenty of surprise interventions where no player has asked for, say, a handball.

With only one missed VAR intervention, according to the Key Match Incidents Panel, in the Premier League this season, the video referees will argue they are getting the balance right.

Iraola clearly will not share that sentiment today.

articles.title: "El Atlético es el gran tapado para ganar la Liga"
articles.standfirst: 'El Corrillo' es el tiempo de opinión de Directo MARCA
articles.summary: 'El Corrillo' es el tiempo de opinión de Directo MARCA
articles.body: Jorge López Marco 'Tote', Juanma Prieto, Santi Siguero y Manel Bruña debaten sobre la actualidad deportiva en 'El Corrillo' de Directo MARCA junto a Rafa Sahuquillo. Con la jornada de Liga como punto central del debate. El Atlético de Madrid ha dejado de ser un aspirante silencioso para convertirse en una alternativa real al título de Liga. La victoria ante el Valencia y el buen momento de los de Simeone han reforzado su candidatura antes de una semana decisiva, con el Bayern de Múnich en Champions y el Barcelona en el Metropolitano. "El Atleti es el gran tapado para ganar la Liga este año", aseguró Manel Bruña, periodista de Mundo Deportivo, durante la tertulia de Radio Marca. El conjunto rojiblanco podría asaltar el liderato en solitario si vence al Barça este domingo, en un duelo directo que promete marcar el pulso del campeonato. Las sensaciones que transmite el equipo convencen también a sus exfutbolistas. Jorge López Marco, Tote, destacó la solidez y la ambición de los colchoneros: "Me da sensación de equipo. Defensivamente, seis veces en lo que va de Liga con la portería a cero, muy importante porque el Atleti, si ahí es fuerte, puede competir con cualquiera". El exjugador puso en valor la llegada de Cuti Romero, la progresión de Baena y Julián Alvarez y el talento de Giuliano Simeone, además de una plantilla que cuenta con alternativas de nivel. "Este año hay ambición y la segunda línea te llega a rematar. Es un equipo que puede estar mejor o peor, pero te genera porque tiene ambición por ganar, porque no tiene miedo y no sale a especular", añadió Tote. Juanma Prieto también considera que el Atlético atraviesa un momento ideal para confirmar sus aspiraciones: "Creo que este año se lo están creyendo. Ya no tienen esa irregularidad que tenían otros años, que podían ganar al Madrid y a la semana siguiente perder con uno de abajo". El exdelantero ve en los próximos encuentros una oportunidad para dar un golpe encima de la mesa y demostrar que los rojiblancos pueden competir por todo. Con el Barcelona y el Bayern como grandes exámenes inmediatos, el Atlético tiene ante sí la posibilidad de transformar las buenas sensaciones en una candidatura firme al título. "No vería muy raro que el Atlético ganase la Liga este año", sentenció Bruña.
