articles.title: Oliver Glasner: Nottingham Forest hierarchy welcome strong reaction from head coach after Brentford defeat
articles.summary: Nottingham Forest are 19th in the Premier League and lost to Brentford on Saturday; Oliver Glasner had an angry reaction afterwards, vowing to make changes at the club or be sacked; however, the club's hierarchy have welcomed the outburst and will stick with the Austrian head coach
articles.body:
Sources at the club are impressed by his determination to get Forest out of their current slump and insist it is "business as usual" following the criticism he levelled at some of his players.

Glasner said there would be "no more hugs" after his side slipped to 19th in the Premier League with Saturday's 2-0 defeat at Brentford.

Having departed Crystal Palace, Glasner was hired in the summer in an attempt to bring stability to the City Ground, after they got through four different head coaches last season.

The Austrian is promising "changes" following his side's poor start to the campaign - something that is expected to be a key point of discussion when he speaks to the media again on Thursday.

Glasner has already had a huge influence off the field at Forest, with only three senior players coming in this summer at his insistence.

After the loss in West London, he said: "We have to accept it's not good enough. If we lose four of the last five games, it's not good enough. And that's why for me, it's now time that we change things, that I change things, and that's what I will do.

"I feel now maybe I made too many compromises in some stuff, and it's always compromises. It's a clear way. I will tell [the players] what we want to do, what we have to do, and if the players buy in, I think we can have a turnaround, and if not, the sixth manager [since the start of last season] will come in."

Glasner says 'either you buy in to changes or you leave'

After the weekend's defeat to Brentford, Glasner added that he was not concerned for his job, adding he was committed to helping Forest change across the board.

He said: "I have no consequences. I think you see that. For me, I go home and have breakfast with my family. It's not the worst situation. Nobody needs to have pity with Oliver Glasner or with the manager. If I want, I could start in two weeks somewhere else. I won't do it.

"But, you know, the players, the staff, they remain in the same situation. And it's the same, sorry for the word, s*** situation that the club had last year.

"So you need to change and rebuild from the bottom to the top. And this is clear for me. And this is what I will do. And without any compromises. Zero. Zero. And if these things don't work, they will let me know [about my exit].

"I didn't come to Nottingham because I was bored at home. No, I came to Nottingham to succeed. I came to Nottingham to get the visions of the owner and the fans and the club to reality. And therefore we need to have a bigger change than maybe I thought, to be honest.

"But again, when you're in a club, then you see what's going on. And I'm desperate to get this tournament around.

"But again, Oliver Glasner can't do anything alone. And I said this so often, and not just after a defeat. I always said the same after winning.

"It's not me, no, but we're all together and can do it. But I know where we have to go. And therefore, it's exactly this, being ruthless. And either you buy in or you leave. It's the only way.

"There is no compromise. Either you buy in where we want to go as a club. Because, and I mentioned it, if you're three times struggling, four or five Premier League seasons, struggling, being at the bottom of the league, there is a pattern.

"And I just know that Oliver Glasner is not here for five years."

articles.title: El final más doloroso de la buena racha
articles.standfirst: La derrota con polémica en San Mamés, por el penalti señalado contra la Real, puso fin a la serie de cuatro triunfos seguidos y dejó sin récord personal a Matarazzo
articles.summary: La derrota con polémica en San Mamés, por el penalti señalado contra la Real, puso fin a la serie de cuatro triunfos seguidos y dejó sin récord personal a Matarazzo
articles.body: La derrota en San Mamés supuso el final de la gran racha que la Real Sociedad estaba protagonizando en LaLiga, con cuatro victorias consecutivas que le habían aupado hasta la quinta posición, y en general en la temporada, ya que a esos resultados en el torneo de la regularidad había añadido un empate y un triunfo en una Europa League en la que también se ha acercado a los puestos de arriba. Los de Pellegrino Matarazzo no caían desde el 17 de septiembre, por 1-2 frente al Bournemouth en Anoeta. La derrota contra el equipo inglés, tras una muy mala primera parte, supuso el punto de inflexión de la Real, que luego venció 2-3 en Mestalla antes de un parón internacional del que regresó superando 3-2 al Dépor, empatando en la visita europea al USG, goleando 2-5 al Málaga y 0-6 al Lillestrom, y venciendo con solvencia 2-1 al Levante. Habían sido cuatro triunfos consecutivos en LaLiga de una Real que era el tercer mejor equipo desde la tercera jornada, lo que le hizo colocarse quinta en la clasificación, una posición que aún mantiene y con cierta renta sobre algunos rivales en la pelea por los puestos europeos a los que hubiera metido hasta 10 puntos de haberse llevado los de San Mamés, como al propio Athletic, al Celta o al mismísimo Villarreal. Además, Matarazzo se queda sin superar su tope como técnico de cuatro victorias seguidas en Liga. La Real debe centrarse ahora en vencer este jueves al Olympique de Lyon para acercarse la top 8 de la Europa League, un encuentro que se jugará en Anoeta, donde el domingo llegará el Rayo Vallecano, al que derrotarle supondría dejar lo de Bilbao en sólo un mal resultado. Después llegará el parón y luego Racing de Santander, Sevilla, Villarreal y Getafe, en otra serie de encuentros que pueden marcar en la pelra por la zona continental de LaLiga.

articles.title: Maroan no volverá a jugar hasta diciembre...y todavía puede ser peor
articles.standfirst: El delantero sufre una lesión de carácter moderado-severo en la musculatura isquiotibial
articles.summary: El delantero sufre una lesión de carácter moderado-severo en la musculatura isquiotibial
articles.body: maroan, una de las apuestas de Terzic para jugar en punta, no volverá a jugar hasta diciembre tras la lesión que sufrió en el derbi con la Real. El atacante gasteiztarra, aunque es internacional con Marruecos al disponer de doble nacionalidad, se fue entre lágrimas al poco de comenzar el partido. Y tenía su por qué: sufre una lesión moderada-severa en la musculatura isquiotibial de la pierna izquierda. Causará baja segura en los partidos de Liga ante Osasuna, Espanyol y Málaga y a partir de ahí mandará la evolución. En diciembre el Athletic jugará frente a Real Madrid, Rayo, Deportivo y Betis. El atacante había ganado presencia en las alineaciones de Terzic, que en la última ventana FIFA probó con Maroan en ataque en el derbi que decidió la Euskal Herria Txapela. Fue protagonista porque el Athletic ganó con un gol suyo. El delantero veía la luz después de que la pasada temporada, tras jugar varias semanas mermado, tuviera que pasar por el quirófano para solucionar un problema de rodilla. Maroan se lastimó en el primer minuto tras caerle encima Sarr, que había ido al bulto y arrolló al delantero del Athletic. El percance fue a más y poco tiempo después, al tratar de iniciar una carrera, sintió que le era imposible. Se fue al vestuario con lágrimas y el consuelo de médicos y entrenadores. La lesión de Maroan obligará a Terzic a buscar alternativas para el 4-4-2 que había dispuesto ante Getafe y Real. Berenguer, Sancet y Robert Navarro son posibilidades para jugar haciendo pareja con Iñaki Williams. La ausencia del gasteiztarra provocará que Txus Vizcay, que ya ha debutado en Liga y también marcado en Copa, repita en las convocatorias y aumente su posibilidad de minutos.

articles.title: Barcelona vs Aston Villa: Champions League – Predictions, news, lineups
articles.summary: Aston Villa, second in the UEFA Champions League table after three wins from three, head to Barcelona, three points back
articles.body:
Who : Barcelona vs Aston Villa What : UEFA Champions League, matchday 4 When : Tuesday, November 2, 20:00 GMT Where : Spotify Camp Nou, Barcelona, Spain How to follow : Al Jazeera will provide build-up and live updates from 17:00 GMT.

It’s a big match in the fledgling UEFA Champions League standings, with Aston Villa seeking to extend their perfect start to the league phase with a daunting trip to Barcelona.

Star-studded Barca are among the favourites to win the competition and sit top of La Liga after 10 wins from 11 matches. But they are eighth in the league phase table after seeing their perfect start to the campaign ended by a 4-2 defeat at PSG in their most recent fixture.

Though their domestic campaign has been slow to get going, Villa have won all three games, scoring 12 goals in Europe and will be keen to repeat their progress to the quarterfinals from 2024-25, when they went out narrowly against eventual winners PSG.

It’s another huge milestone on an impressive journey for Villa, who are owned by V Sports, a holding company jointly controlled by Egyptian billionaire Nassef Sawiris and US private equity investor Wes Edens.

They completed their takeover of the Birmingham-based club in 2019, following the club’s promotion back to the Premier League after three seasons in the Championship.

Three bottom-half finishes followed but after Unai Emery was appointed in October 2022 following the departure of Steven Gerrard, the Spaniard guided Villa to seventh place at the end of that season and qualification for the UEFA Conference League, their first European campaign in well over a decade.

England striker Ollie Watkins – now playing for Saudi side Al-Hilal – scored 27 goals as Emery’s side reached the semifinals and also secured a top-four finish in the Premier League, securing Champions League football for the first time and their first appearance in Europe’s top competition in 41 years.

A famous 1-0 win over Bayern Munich at Villa Park and a goalless draw with Juventus helped them progress to the quarterfinals where they were edged out by eventual champions PSG, despite Villa winning the second leg 3-2 at Villa Park.

A sixth-placed finish in the Premier League saw Villa qualify for the Europa League last season and they swept through the group stage, winning seven of their eight games, before beating Lille, Bologna and Nottingham Forest in the knockouts and breezing past Freiburg 3-0 in Istanbul in May to lift the trophy.

Another top-four Premier League finish came alongside it and took Emery’s side back into Europe’s top competition where they will now play on one of the biggest stages in world football, seeking to show they belong there.

While Hansi Flick’s side will start as strong favourites, they have not kept a clean sheet in the Champions League in 18 games – the longest run of any team in this season’s edition – and Villa will have their eye on writing another chapter in their fairytale story of recent seasons.

After a perfect start to the campaign with thumping wins over Feyenoord and at Galatasaray, Hansi Flick’s side lost an epic Champions League encounter 4-2 against PSG to suffer their first defeat.

A 2-1 home loss to Real Madrid followed four days later in El Clasico, which ended their perfect start to their La Liga campaign after nine straight wins.

Barca, however, returned to winning ways by thrashing Alaves 6-1 on Saturday to return to the top of the table after briefly being overhauled by Atletico Madrid.

Lamine Yamal scored one and set up another, meaning he has notched 12 goals and 11 assists in all competitions this season. He already holds the record for Champions League assists by a teenager with 13, and is surely bound to find the single goal he needs in order to add the goals record before he turns 20 in July.

It’s been an up-and-down start to the campaign for the Villans.

They are only kept off the top of the league phase table by Paris Saint-Germain – who beat them 2-1 in the UEFA Super Cup in August after Villa’s Europa League win last season.

The English club sit second by virtue of goals scored alone after winning 3-2 at Club Brugge, 6-0 at home to Fenerbahce and then 3-1 against Viking at Villa Park.

However, in the Premier League they claimed one point from their opening four matches, though Saturday’s 1-1 draw against lowly Fulham, in which keeper Zion Suzuki scored an own goal, extended their unbeaten run to five games from which they have taken 11 points to climb to ninth.

They were dumped out of the English League Cup 3-0 by Bournemouth last week in the last-16 and announced on Saturday they will pursue legal action ⁠⁠against pundit Jamie ⁠⁠Carragher. Villa are accusing the former Liverpool defender of making “unacceptable insults” about the ⁠⁠club and their supporters, saying “Aston Villa will never be Manchester United”, suggesting there is a hierarchy in football.

Barcelona defeated Aston Villa in 72.0% of the Opta supercomputer’s 10,000 pre-match simulations, making them comfortable favourites for all three points.

Villa’s 100% start to the competition is therefore expected to end, with the away side pulling off a shock win in just 12.7% of the simulations and snatching a draw in 15.3%.

This will be their first meeting since the European Super Cup final in January 1983. Villa were 3-1 winners on aggregate but suffered a 1-0 loss at Camp Nou in the first encounter.

The second leg was their fourth meeting in all competitions and Villa’s 3-0 success represented their first victory against Barca.

Unai Emery has much more recent history with the Catalans, though. He has faced them 30 times throughout his managerial career and picked up just three victories (D6 L21). His win percentage of 10% against Barca is his lowest against any side he has faced at least five times.

Emery suffered his heaviest ever loss in European competition at Barca when his Paris Saint-Germain side lost 6-1 at Camp Nou in March 2017, a match famously dubbed La Remontada .

(Last five games in all competitions; latest match first)

Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick : “I’m focused on the next match. This is a Champions League match, and Aston Villa is in great form and Unai Emery is one of the best coaches in Europe. We’re talking about the Champions League… Every match is special. Any opponent has the quality to cause you problems; it will be a very difficult match.

“At this level, anything can happen. Against Real Madrid, the result could have been different. We have confidence in these kinds of matches, we really do. We’ve won 11 games, only two losses… I have confidence in the team and we showed that last Saturday. Now we’re talking about the Champions League and we’re focused on finishing among the top eight.”

Barcelona and England winger Anthony Gordon : “Aston Villa are a very good team. I’ve played against them a couple of times. They have one of the best managers in the world and some very good players. They’re in great form and it’s going to be a great game. They’re always fully engaged, so it’s going to be quite a challenge.”

While their attack has been rampant, Barca have been beset by defensive problems due to injuries to Eric Garcia, Jules Kounde and Xavi Espart. Those personnel issues forced Flick to hand Brian Farinas a debut at right-back and deploy Frenkie de Jong in the centre of defence at the weekend.

Andreas Christensen will not be risked despite stepping up his recovery from a thigh injury by returning to training.

Barcelona : Joan García, Joao Cancelo, Gerard Martín, Pau Cubarsi, Alejandro Balde, Fermin Lopez, Rodri, Pedri, Lamine Yamal, Raphinha, Anthony Gordon.

There are no new injury concerns for Unai Emery to contend with, though Amadou Onana, Matteo Ruggeri and Aaron Wan-Bissaka remain absent.

Aston Villa: Zion Suzuki, Matty Cash, Viktor Lindelof, Pau Torres, Ian Maatsen, Boubacar Kamara, Joao Gomes, John McGinn, Johan Manzambi, Emiliano Buendia, Nicolas Jackson.

articles.title: El Madrid se frota las manos con su campeón del mundo de 15 años, 1,92 metros y ¡148! goles
articles.standfirst: El delantero Mikel López es una de las joyas de la corona de La Fábrica
articles.summary: El club renueva al delantero Mikel López, una de las joyas de la corona de La Fábrica y acechado por los grandes de media Europa
articles.body: El Real Madrid tiene un pequeño 'Haaland' en La Fábrica. Un prodigio del gol con un físico imponente. Las mismas dos características que encumbraron desde muy joven a la estrella del City. Mikel López, delantero centro del Cadete A y desde el pasado viernes campeón del mundo sub 15 (junto a los también madridistas Alberto Ruiz y Adrián Bielsa), es una de las grandes joyas de la corona de la cantera madridista, a la que el club está cuidando como oro en paño. Por ello el Madrid blindó hace un año al prometedor ariete de 15 años, 1,92 metros de altura y ¡148 goles! en las cinco temporadas que lleva en el Real Madrid. Una edad, envergadura y cifra goleadora que lo convierten en un 'cañón' a pesar de estar aún lejos de los filiales más estratégicos y decisivos. Mikel López es una gran apuesta de futuro del Real Madrid y de ahí la renovación que firmó en noviembre de 2025 para alejar a otros clubes que lo tienen en su radar. Al menos, de momento, porque la gran prueba de fuego llegará cuando el delantero cumpla los 16 años en 2027 y pueda firmar su primer contrato profesional. Mikel López es una máquina perfecta de marcar. El año pasado marcó 37 goles con el Cadete B. La temporada 24-25, en el Infantil A, se convirtió en el mejor goleador de toda La Fábrica, firmando 43 goles de los 138 que anotó su equipo para coronarse campeón de Liga. Además, 38 goles marcó en la 23-24 (Infantil B) y otros 30 en la 22-23 (Alevín A), su primera temporada de madridista tras llegar procedente del Canillas para incorporarse al Alevín A. Un ritmo goleador frenético que ya le permitió superar el listón de los 100 goles en marzo de 2025, tras marcar al Fuenlabrada. En total como madridista, 148 goles. La misma proyección imparable que tiene en el Madrid la lleva también en la selección, donde ya es internacional sub 16, con la que se estrenó en septiembre en dos amistosos contra Italia. Antes ya ha sido un habitual en la sub 15, con la que ha ganado el reciente Mundial, marcando 6 goles en el torneo, de la categoría y con la que previamente había disputado 11 encuentros, marcando 6 goles. A pesar del privilegiado físico que tiene y que le permite ser tremendamente dominante en el área, Mikel López posee una gran cantidad de cualidades que le permiten multiplicar sus prestaciones ofensivas. No sólo es un chico alto, es un buen jugador. Tiene una gran coordinación en sus movimientos y es rápido, se maneja muy bien con el balón porque tiene calidad y atesora un gran sentido del juego, lo que le permite tener también unas buenas estadísticas en asistencias. Juega bien y se asocia bien. Mikel López es más que un rematador, su gran especialidad porque maneja todos los registros de un 'killer'. Tiene buen disparo y en el juego aéreo es imparable y casi infalible.

articles.title: Carrick not distracted by speculation over United future
articles.summary: Manchester United coach says his players remain committed to the cause despite nine-match winless run
articles.body:
Under-fire Manchester United boss Michael Carrick says speculation about his future will not impact their Champions League game against Roma.

United are winless in nine matches, their worst run in 38 years, and sit outside the Premier League relegation zone on goal difference with just one win and seven points from their opening nine fixtures.

Saturday’s 2-0 defeat at Chelsea increased speculation that Tuesday night’s visit of Roma in their fourth Champions League league phase match might be his last, given the Giallorossi’s unbeaten start in Serie A and 16 goals across their past four matches, with their only defeat of the season coming in Real Madrid’s dramatic 4-3 win in the Stadio Olimpico on October 14 .

Speaking at his pre-match media conference, Carrick said: “(Speculation) has no influence on how we prepare or on the game. We cannot wait for it. That is all I am focused on. What happens after, happens. Whatever direction it goes in.”

Carrick said he believes the players remain committed to the cause, despite the manner of their defeat at Stamford Bridge, with Lisandro Martinez’s quickfire sending-off and penalty concession ending their hopes of a comeback.

“I know what we are capable of. We have shown it in bursts, (including) the other day. We are close but need to act on it quickly.

“I have no concerns about (Martinez’s) commitment. Things happen in football. Sometimes you make mistakes. The commitment is not an issue.

“The dressing room is in a good place. The commitment of the players to the club, to me, to each other – do not question it at all. We need to play better, we can make better decisions, but the commitment is not a thing at all.

“We have to find a way out of this moment. We have done a lot of good things, we just couldn’t capitalise on it, but we will do. We have to keep doing the right things.

“A lot of people could do my job when you are winning games. It is about finding solutions, finding answers, staying strong, leading right and getting the best out of the players and we have to keep pushing for that.

“I love being here, I love working with the players. The struggles, the challenges, that just drives you on to want even more,” Carrick said.

United’s only win since August came in the 4-0 success against Sabah at Old Trafford on September 10 but another against Roma would keep United’s hopes of progressing to the knockout stages alive, said Carrick.

“We are looking for the win. There is the bigger picture and it is about getting through to the later stages.

“One or two (defeats) you can get away with… as long as you make amends for that. There are times, like tomorrow, that are going to dictate that for us. We’re certainly still in it. We’ve a great chance of progressing and that has to be the focus from now.”

Midfielder Kobbie Mainoo also gave his backing to the head coach and said the players have to fight as one to get through this ‘bump in the road’.

“I have been at this club for a long time and I know there’s always going to be ups and downs, it’s never going to be plain sailing to the top so you expect bumps and the best thing about it is that you’re able to bounce back from them.”

“I feel like our way to repay the manager is to be behind him on and off the pitch and fight as a team.

“I’m grateful to the boss for putting trust in me as soon as he came in and giving me all the advice that he has, knowing that he’s been a player and knows the history of this club and what it takes to win.

“I take those words to heart and try to apply them every day.”

articles.title: 9 Florida State head coach candidates to replace Mike Norvell, ranked
articles.summary: These are the coaches Florida State should go after in football.
articles.body:
After weeks of speculation , it finally happened.

Following a 36-24 loss to Clemson, Florida State parted ways with Mike Norvell. The firing closes the book on his tenure in Tallahassee, which included a 13-1 finish in 2023 that had the Seminoles on the cusp of the College Football Playoff, but the team was left out by the Selection Committee following a season-ending injury to starting quarterback Jordan Travis.

Since that season, Florida State limped to a pair of losing seasons, and the writing was on the wall for Norvell.

Here are nine candidates to replace him, ranked by likelihood.

On the one hand, you can see the appeal here. This reads like something straight out of a Hollywood script: The former player returns to campus to take over as head coach. Deion Sanders was a three-sport star at Florida State, most known for what he did in the fall on the football field but he stood out on the diamond as well as on the track. In May of 1987, for example, Sanders played in two conference tournament baseball games while running a leg of the 4 x 100 relay, all on the same day.

But some of the shine is off his coaching resume, as Colorado has struggled the past season-plus. After leading the Buffaloes to a 9-4 record in 2024, when he coached Heisman Trophy winner Travis Hunter Jr., Colorado finished 3-9 in 2025, and is on pace for another losing season this year.

It would make for a good story, albeit an unlikely one.

8. Jimbo Fisher — Former head coach, FSU/Texas A&M

And now we have another unlikely return to Tallahassee.

Jimbo Fisher has made no secret of his desire to get back into coaching, and he did deliver a title during his previous stint at Florida State. He also led the Seminoles to five consecutive ten-win seasons and three conference titles during his time on campus.

But his departure from Tallahassee might have left some bitter feelings at Florida State, and his time at Texas A&M could also work against him.

If FSU wants to turn to an up-and-coming head coach, they could stay in-state and hire Zach Kittley from Florida Atlantic.

Kittley has yet to finish his second season as a head coach (he took over at FAU for the 2025 season) but after leading the Owls to a 4-8 record a year ago, he has the school on a path to a winning record — and a bowl bid — here in 2026. And his background as an offensive coach and quarterback developer would work in his favor. Kittley coached Bailey Zappe both at Houston Baptist (where he was the offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach) and later at Western Kentucky, helping Zappe set several NCAA records.

It would be a huge leap, but a bold one, for a program looking for an identity on the offensive side of the ball.

6. Kenny Dillingham — Head coach, Arizona State

Kenny Dillingham is in a pretty good position out at Arizona State, and his ties to Norvell might be enough to dissuade him for a job at Florida State.

But Dillingham also spent some time at FSU (under Norvell) and knows the environment, and what it takes to be successful at Florida State. His experience at schools like Auburn and Oregon works in his favor, as does Arizona State's run to the College Football Playoff in 2024.

Rhett Lashlee is in a tremendous spot at SMU, backed by trustees with resources at his disposal.

Would he walk away from that and jump into the frying pan in Tallahassee?

Under his guidance, the Mustangs have gone 44-17, including a 30-6 record in conference play. SMU has reached a bowl game in every year of his tenure, and at 6-1 the Mustangs are likely headed to another bowl game this year, if not a potential second Playoff berth under his leadership. He is in a very good spot right now, and it might be tough to see him leave what is a strong ACC program for a more turbulent environment in the conference.

But from FSU's perspective, hiring him away from a conference rival makes a great deal of sense.

4. Glenn Schumann — Defensive coordinator, Georgia

Historically, Florida State has favored coaches with an offensive background. Larry Jones, the former South Carolina defensive coordinator, was the last head coaching hire with a pure defensive background at Florida State.

Glenn Schumann could change that. His name has been on the short list of candidates the past few hiring cycles, and Kirby Smart advocated for him to get the UNC job back in 2024, ahead of the eventual Bill Belichick hiring. But Schumann's time under Smart and Nick Saban works in his favor, and one has to believe this is the year he jumps to the head coaching ranks.

3. Eliah Drinkwitz — Head coach, Missouri

Since taking over in Columbia, Eliah Drinkwitz has turned the Tigers into one of the SEC's more intriguing teams. Missouri has reached a bowl game in every year of his tenure, and after winning 11 games in 2023 and ten games in 2024, the Tigers are on pace to have double-digit wins again this year.

But one cannot help but wonder if Drinkwitz has hit the ceiling of what is possible in the SEC, in a conference dominated by big schools such as LSU, Alabama, and more. If he wants to jump at a chance to be a bigger fish in the pond, FSU presents a tremendous opportunity.

2. Jake Dickert — Head coach, Wake Forest

When the Norvell news broke, Jake Dickert's name was one of the first on everyone's mind.

Wake Forest finished with a 9-4 record a year ago, and the Demon Deacons are currently 7-1 and ranked inside the top 15 in the nation. And he has won everywhere he has gone, leaving Washington State with a 23-20 record, and he is currently 16-5 during his two years at Wake Forest.

He also works well with his current general manager, Rob Schlaeger, and their process of identifying talent and recruiting players to campus would work well in the ACC.

On paper, he might be the best option for Florida State, were it not for another former Seminole.

Is FSU interested in a different former Seminole coach, who just led a conference rival to the ACC title?

Diaz attended Florida State, graduating with a communications degree in 1995, and broke through in the coaching ranks as a graduate assistant under Bobby Bowden. That put him on the path to coaching that included stops at NC State, Texas, Mississippi State, Miami, and Penn State, with his first head coaching job coming with the Hurricanes.

But he has done his best work at Duke, leading the Blue Devils to a pair of nine-win seasons in 2024 and 2025, and a year ago Duke was a surprise ACC Championship Game winner. He knows Florida, he knows the conference, and he could be the perfect candidate to turn things around in Tallahassee.

articles.title: Carrick shrugs off Man Utd sack threat and ‘can’t wait’ for Roma clash
articles.summary: Michael Carrick does not feel like his time in the Old Trafford hotseat is running out and is relishing the chance to end Manchester United’s wretched winles...
articles.body:
Michael Carrick does not feel like his time in the Old Trafford hotseat is running out and is relishing the chance to end Manchester United's wretched winless run against Roma in the Champions League.

The head coach's position was hanging by a thread even before Saturday's 2-0 Premier League loss at Chelsea, which meant they sit above the relegation zone on goal difference alone.

United have made their worst start to a league campaign in 40 years and are without a victory in nine matches in all competitions, stretching back to September's 4-0 triumph against Sabah in the Champions League.

The Red Devils play their first home European match since then against in-form Roma on Tuesday, with an Old Trafford encounter against Aston Villa following before an international break that could see a change in the dugout.

Asked if he felt like a coach who only has two matches left having overseen United's worst winless streak since 1988, Carrick said: "No, not at all.

"Listen, I can't look into the future. You never know what's going to happen, I don't know what's going to happen.

"That doesn't change the way I feel, how we're preparing for the game tomorrow, and I'm actually really looking forward to the game. Can't wait for the game tomorrow.

"You might think I'm crazy with the results we've had and what's going on, but I genuinely really can't wait for the game tomorrow, and that's all I'm focused on. Really, I am.

"Whatever happens is going to happen after that in whatever direction it goes in, but we want to make it a big night tomorrow night first."

Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann are contenders to replace Carrick if the much-criticised United hierarchy decide to make a change.

The Glazers and co-owner Jim Ratcliffe are under the microscope along with Ineos appointments such as director of football Jason Wilcox, who Lisandro Martínez critiqued in jaw-dropping fashion three weeks ago.

The United centre-back ended a dramatic month by giving away a penalty and being sent off in the weekend loss at Chelsea, meaning he will be banned for Villa but can feature against Roma.

Carrick said of hot-headed, out-of-sorts defender Martinez: "No, I've got no concerns about commitment at all.

"Things happen in football. Sometimes you do things, sometimes you make a decision, sometimes you make mistakes, sometimes it goes well for you. But the commitment is not an issue for sure."

Speaking on the wider dressing-room culture, the United boss added: "I've said it before, the commitment of the players to the club, to me, to each other, I don't question that at all.

"We need to play better, we can make better decisions, but commitment's not a thing (to worry about) at all."

Marcus Rashford and Luke Shaw will again be unavailable to face Roma through injury, although the former could return from a hip issue to face his former loan club Villa.

Long-term absentees Benjamin Sesko and Manuel Ugarte will miss the Roma encounter, as will Patrick Dorgu despite training on Monday for the first time since sustaining a hamstring injury in September.

United boss Carrick said: "It's great to have him back. He's worked ever so hard to be back with the group but he won't be involved tomorrow. We'll see how he progresses through the week."

articles.title: Chuki, el español que brilla en el resurgir del Werder Bremen
articles.standfirst: El ex del Valladolid pone la magia en el club alemán que con Fullkrug como goleador ha vuelto a los puestos de honor de la Bundesliga
articles.summary: El ex del Valladolid pone la magia en el club alemán que con Fullkrug como goleador ha vuelto a los puestos de honor de la Bundesliga
articles.body: Durante un tramo de la tarde del sábado, el Werder Bremen ocupó puestos de Champions League junto a Bayern de Múnich, Borussia Dortmund y RB Leipzig. Una fotografía provisional de la clasificación, pero también un reflejo del momento que atraviesa el equipo. Al margen de la lucha por el título, la Bundesliga ofrece un escenario abierto, con espacio para que proyectos bien construidos encuentren su sitio entre los grandes. En Bremen vuelven a disfrutar del fútbol y de un equipo que ha recuperado buena parte de su atractivo. Hay razones para el optimismo. El Werder cuenta con el máximo goleador del campeonato, Niclas Füllkrug, autor de nueve tantos; con el máximo asistente, Marco Grüll, extremo que ha repartido siete pases de gol; y con talentos emergentes como Chuki. El mediapunta español, de 22 años, ha encontrado una acogida inmejorable en Alemania y se ha convertido en una pieza fija del once de Daniel Thioune. El técnico le ha entregado la zona del diez, el espacio desde el que puede interpretar el juego, recibir entre líneas y poner su talento al servicio del equipo. Chuki llegó libre desde el Valladolid y está respondiendo con fútbol a la confianza depositada en él. En septiembre fue nominado a mejor rookie del mes y su influencia no ha dejado de crecer. El Werder apostó por su incorporación convencido de que podía crecer de su mano. También había una cuestión de identidad: recuperar la tradición de mediapuntas jóvenes que encontraron en Bremen el escenario para proyectarse hacia la élite. Desde Diego a Mesut Özil, pasando por Kevin De Bruyne, el club ha disfrutado de futbolistas capaces de darle un sentido diferente a su juego. Chuki representa una nueva posibilidad. El pucelano ha encontrado un equipo a su medida. Su adaptación futbolística avanza a gran velocidad, pero también está siendo decisivo el funcionamiento colectivo que rodea su fútbol. Füllkrug pone los goles y castiga a las defensas rivales desde el eje del ataque. Grüll marca diferencias desde el sector izquierdo, mientras Arthur se ha adueñado de todo el carril derecho. En la retaguardia, Amos Pieper aporta mando y estabilidad. Cada pieza tiene su espacio y su función. Y Chuki dispone de un contexto que le permite concentrarse en lo que mejor sabe hacer: dar continuidad a los ataques, encontrar espacios y golpear cerca del área. La recuperación del modelo El Werder ha conseguido reunir una plantilla con perfiles de edades y experiencias diferentes. Hay futbolistas jóvenes, jugadores que atraviesan el mejor momento de su carrera, incorporaciones bien elegidas y cesiones que han aportado soluciones. El resultado es un grupo con recursos, profundidad y una combinación de talento y madurez que empieza a dar sus frutos. No es una cuestión de nombres aislados, sino de encaje. El equipo tiene gol, imaginación, recorrido y una estructura que permite que sus futbolistas más creativos puedan expresarse. La recuperación del proyecto tiene, además, una dimensión histórica. El Werder fue una de las grandes potencias del fútbol alemán, campeón de la Bundesliga y habitual protagonista en las competiciones europeas. Durante años, su presencia en la Champions League formó parte de su paisaje natural. Pero el club perdió altura, se fue alejando de aquella condición y terminó atrapado en una etapa de mediocridad deportiva que culminó con el descenso a la Bundesliga 2 en 2021. Volver a reconocerse entre los equipos importantes del campeonato exigía algo más que una buena temporada. Necesitaba recuperar una idea de club y una manera de competir.

articles.title: Kyle Whittingham says Tommy Carr is Michigan's starting QB for Michigan State game, 'forseeable future'
articles.summary: Carr has gone 1-1 as Michigan's starting QB so far.
articles.body:
On Monday, University of Michigan head football coach Kyle Whittingham discussed the Wolverines' quarterback situation at his weekly press conference.

Whittingham confirmed Carr will start this weekend against Michigan State and for the "foreseeable future."

Michigan started the year with Bryce Underwood under center, but switched to true freshman Tommy Carr three weeks ago during the Penn State game. Underwood has since come in for certain plays, but Carr has led the offense.

Carr has started two games so far this season, taking over after halftime against the Nittany Lions. He has completed 47 of his 66 passes for 480 yards with a touchdown and an interception. Carr has been an effective runner with 96 yards and three touchdowns on the ground.

Underwood has played in seven games so far this year. He has thrown for 924 yards with five touchdowns and six interceptions. Underwood has been a solid runner, picking up 222 yards and two scores on 61 carries.

Michigan had a scare against Rutgers last week, winning just 28-21. The Wolverines took the lead with 4:24 left after Carr punched in a nine-yard rushing touchdown.

The quarterback finished the win with 266 passing yards, 1 passing touchdown, 54 rushing yards and 2 rushing touchdowns.

On Monday, Whittingham said that he loved everything he saw from Carr last Saturday and that the quarterback played a complete game . He also said Carr's rushing ability was key to the win.

Carr will meet Michigan State for the first time in the Battle for the Paul Bunyan Trophy on Saturday.

After that, Michigan ends the season with Oregon, No. 5 UCLA, and No. 11 Ohio State needing one more win over their final four games to become bowl-eligible.

articles.title: Folarin Balogun scores first goal since starring for USMNT at World Cup
articles.summary: For the first time since his breakout 2026 World Cup, USMNT striker Folarin Balogun has scored a goal, his first for Monaco.
articles.body:
For the first time since his breakout 2026 World Cup , Folarin Balogun has scored a goal.

Balogun came on as a halftime substitute for Monaco against Paris FC on Sunday, Nov. 1. The American striker found the net from close range in the 65th minute, cutting Paris FC's lead to 2-1.

The home side would eventually add a third goal, defeating Monaco 3-1.

But for Balogun, the goal was still a positive sign following a tumultuous few months after starring for the U.S. men's national team at the World Cup on home soil.

Balogun was caught up in a hugely controversial incident following his red card in a 2-0 win against Bosnia and Herzegovina in the World Cup round of 32 – also the last game he scored in before Sunday.

USMNT shines in September-October international window

The forward's automatic suspension was reversed the day before the USMNT faced Belgium in the round of 16, surprisingly giving the U.S. back one of its most crucial players.

Shortly after FIFA's decision was announced, President Donald Trump revealed he pushed FIFA president Gianni Infantino to reverse the suspension. Even with Balogun involved, the U.S. was hammered 4-1 by Belgium.

Following the World Cup, Balogun received interest from several clubs across Europe and was on the verge of joining Everton, before his move to the Premier League side broke down at the 11th hour.

Balogun is still expected to leave Monaco in the near future, perhaps as soon as January. In the meantime, he's seen limited minutes at the Ligue 1 club this season. The 25-year-old dealt with an injury early in the season, before recently being relegated to second choice behind 20-year-old forward Paris Brunner.

Balogun has made just five total appearances this season, coming off the bench in all of them.

articles.title: The 5 best games of men’s college basketball’s opening night
articles.summary: The greatest sport in the world is officially back on Monday, and with the return comes a pretty loaded opening slate. Here’s a quick look at the five best g...
articles.body:
The greatest sport in the world is officially back on Monday, and with the return comes a pretty loaded opening slate.

Here's a quick look at the five best games of college basketball's opening day.

T.J. Otzelberger and company will look to make an early statement that the show will go on without Joshua Jefferson and Milan Momcilovic when they take on Memphis at the Sanford Pentagon in South Dakota.

The Cyclones may have lost their two leading scorers from last season's Sweet 16 squad, but they return the next three in Killyan Toure, Blake Buchanan and Jamarion Bateman. Not many other squads ranked in the preseason top 25 can lay claim to that level of roster retention.

On the other side, Memphis feels like a program at a crossroads. Despite the early excitement, the Penny Hardaway experience has been more bust than boom, and now Hardaway has spent $2.6 million of his own money to fund a roster that seems … just ok. The Tigers can make a big statement to the contrary if they can hang with ISU on opening night.

What was widely referred to as "the most anticipated season in BYU basketball history" wound up being something of a disappointment, as A.J. Dybantsa (despite being as good as advertised) and company lost 12 times and failed to win a game in the NCAA Tournament. Kevin Young will try to accomplish more without the likely No. 1 pick in this summer's NBA Draft, and has the chance to it thanks to the return of point guard Rob Wright and the additions of a deep portal class as well as five-star freshman Bruce Branch III.

The Cougars should be pushed in an entertaining opener against an Ohio State team that features one of the nation's most underrated players in John Mobley Jr. If Justin Pippen and Amare Bynum take steps forward, there's no reason for Jake Diebler not to have an NCAA Tournament team in Columbus.

Purdue is 5-0 all-time against Gonzaga, including a Sweet 16 win in the 2024 NCAA Tournament. If the Zags are gonna notch win No. 1 over Matt Painter's squad, this feels like the year to do it.

In a flip of roles, it's Gonzaga that enters this season expected to feature one of the biggest, baddest frontcourts in the country thanks to the return of Braden Huff and the addition of Arizona State transfer Massamba Diop. Purdue has size as well (per usual), it's just unproven relative to its recent squads. Junior guard C.J. Cox was lights out during exhibition play and will now look to prove in a real contest that a breakout season is on the horizon.

Hooray for the UCLA-Arizona rivalry returning. Less of a hooray for this game being played at a neutral site and not in front of a revved up crowd in Tucson or Westwood. Still, we'll take what we can get, and what we're getting is the 116th all-time meeting in arguably the best West Coast rivalry in the history of the sport.

Arizona looks like a legitimate national title contender thanks in large part to the returns of Motiejus Krivas and Ivan Kharchenkov. The Bruins are less of a known commodity, but have a potential superstar in Nikola Kusturica, a 6'9 wing from Serbia who has the potential to make a large national splash on opening night.

UCLA owns a 64-51 all-time advantage in this series, which dates back to 1923. Bruins head coach Mick Cronin is 7-7 against the Wildcats, with all seven losses coming to current 'Zona head coach Tommy Lloyd.

The showcase game of day one features the preseason No. 1 team in the country taking on a Miami team that more than a few people view as a darkhorse Final Four contender.

The returns of Thomas Haugh, Alex Condon and Rueben Chinyelu give the Gators the best frontcourt in the country, but Miami is one of the few teams on UF's schedule with the size and athleticism necessary to keep up with Todd Golden's team. Malik Reneau is back, and he has significant frontcourt help this season in the form of super athletic sophomore forward Shelton Henderson and Georgia big man transfer Somto Cyril. If Villanova transfer guard Acaden Lewis can be the star Jai Lucas believes he can, Miami could easily be the top challenger to Duke in the ACC.

The last time the No. 1 team in the country lost on opening night? Seven years ago in 2019 when No. 1 Michigan State got toppled by No. 2 Kentucky in the Champions Classic.

articles.title: Joao Félix se luce con un Al Nassr sin Cristiano Ronaldo: dos goles y dos asistencias
articles.standfirst: Triunfo saudí en la Champions de Asia con goleada (2-6) en Uzbekistán
articles.summary: Triunfo saudí en la Champions de Asia con goleada (2-6) en Uzbekistán
articles.body: El nivel de Joao Félix en Arabia Saudí está fuera de toda de duda. Después de generar dobles dígitos en goles y asistencias el pasado curso, con un Al Nassr campeón de liga junto a Cristiano Ronaldo, el luso ha arrancado este curso enchufado. Si venía de dar cuatro asistencias en el 5-3 ante Al Kholood... el partido de hoy en Champions de Asia ha sido otro 'show' del ex Atlético o Barcelona. Dos goles y dos asistencias de Joao en Tashkent para frenar cualquier resistencia del Pakhtakor uzbeko en la Champions de Asia. Al Nassr ganó 2-6 (sin Cristiano Ronaldo, que se quedó en Arabia Saudí) y suma su segundo triunfo en tres partidos en la máxima competición continental. Los 68 minutos que Joao Félix estuvo sobre el terreno de juego fueron un recital. Asistió a Al Hamdan en el 0-1 y a Al Amri en el 1-4... pero también dejó dos goles. El 0-2, con una brillante acción individual que dejó por el suelo a la zaga uzbeka; el 0-3, rematando a gol un buen pase de Sadio Mané. Para el luso ya son siete goles y 11 asistencias en esta 2026-27. De nuevo, camino del 'doble-doble' con Al Nassr.
